description:
Business Development Manager – Oil & Gas Enterprise Technology Solution
Location: Lagos, Nigeria
Industry: Technology
About the Role
Our Client is looking for a driven, results-oriented Business Development Manager to lead the commercial Enterprise/Technology solution for oil and gas industry. This is a high-impact, quota-carrying role for a sales professional who thrives on winning new business, building strategic relationships, and closing enterprise deals.
If you're passionate about fintech, energized by the challenge of opening new markets, and skilled at engaging C-suite decision-makers, we want to hear from you.
What You'll Do
- Own the full sales cycle — from prospecting and lead generation through proposal development, negotiation, and contract closure.
- Drive customer acquisition across sectors including , Manufacturing, Oil & Gas
- Build relationships with key decision-makers — CEOs, CFOs, Treasury - Managers, CIOs.
- Forge strategic partnerships with Manufacturing, Oil and Gas companies
- Manage and grow enterprise accounts, identifying upsell and cross-sell opportunities.
- Represent the company at industry events, conferences, and forums.
- Deliver on targets — consistently meeting and exceeding monthly, quarterly, and annual sales goals.
What You Bring
- 7- 10 years of experience in Business Development, Enterprise Sales, Solution Sales, or FinTech Sales.
- A proven track record of consistently hitting or exceeding sales targets.
- Experience selling enterprise software, SaaS, fintech platforms, or digital transformation solutions.
- Confidence engaging C-suite executives and senior decision-makers.
Strong consultative selling, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
- A Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Finance, Economics, or a related field (MBA is a plus).
Experience with oil and Gas or manufacturing clients is an advantage.
Why Join Us
Work with a collaborative team across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Customer Success.
Competitive compensation with performance-based incentives.
Real ownership over your pipeline, your targets, and your growth.
Qualified and interested candidates should send CV to recruitment@macsuhroutsourcing.com indicating the subject.

Shape the future of energy with VINCI Energies Oil & Gas!
At
VINCI Energies Oil & Gas (VINCI Energies group)
, we empower our clients in the energy sector by delivering end-to-end support across the full lifecycle of their industrial projects, energy infrastructures, and ICT operations.
As a specialized service company, our
2,000 experts operate across five continents
, bringing cutting-edge expertise from design to operation. With 35 agile and locally rooted Business Units, we combine deep field insight with the strength of a global network of trusted brands.
Our diverse business lines include
EPC project delivery, engineering, automation, commissioning, maintenance, training, fire and gas analysis, technical assistance, safety, and cybersecurity.
We proudly serve leading operators in Oil & Gas, Transmission Systems, Electrical Infrastructure, and Renewable Energy—driving innovation and excellence in every project.
Part of the VINCI Energies Group,
Actemium Oil & Gas Maintenance
provides comprehensive maintenance solutions and engineering to ensure the reliability, safety, and performance of critical industrial equipment.
The Opportunity
We are seeking a
CRANE AND LIFTING EQUIPMENT SPECIALIST
to join a major
GMC (General Maintenance Contract) project in Nigeria
.
Job Purpose
This job is created to provide technical and economic leadership in the inspection, maintenance and reliability of cranes and lifting equipment according to safety standards.
General Conditions
Location: Lagos, Nigeria
Work Arrangement: Residential position with the flexibility of a rotational schedule (12 weeks on-site / 4 weeks off), offering an excellent work-life balance.
Start Date:ASAP
Contract Duration: Initial 18-month assignment with strong potential for extension on a long-term project.
JOB DIMENSIONS
To ensure cranes and lifting equipment reliability and availability according to safety standards.
To ensure operational engineering processes, inspection and maintenance are efficiently carried out in strict compliance with safety policies and procedures on all lifting and marine equipment
To ensure crane and lifting equipment support as technical authority to the DW field operations in accordance with Company rules and statutory regulation.
To analyse crane maintenance activities and lifting equipment performance from the technical and economic perspective and take action necessary to achieve company set objectives regarding efficiency, cost optimization and savings.
To provide Marine lifting equipment support to Maintenance Operations Mechanical Static team when required
ACTIVITIES
To prepare all methods support and implementation of practice documents regarding preventative maintenance, inspection, and testing to be performed on AKPO & EGINA cranes and lifting equipment based on recognized best practice and applicable regulations.
To prepare and develop specifications for new cranes and lifting equipment based on recognized international standards.
Co-ordinate planned crane maintenance activities fleet-wide in conjunction with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).
Manage specialized crane maintenance vendors interventions and contracts (Liebherr, Sparrow, National Oilwell Varco etc.) within SCM frame agreements (including technical scope of work) where applicable.
Ensure the implementation and assurance of Company integrity management system compliance.
Liaise with classification societies/third party design offices where applicable.
Support DW TUPNI asset installations for all related crane issues (specifically for new cranes, specification for upgrades and heavy lift works on cranes).
Liaise with crane manufacturers when required.
Participate in and/or lead investigations for all crane related incidents across the fleet.
Interface with DW INSPECTION Department for all crane related issues.
Supervision until completion of 5-years major overhauls in all DW installations cranes (based on Contractor/OEM and CPLO reports).
Follow spare parts stocks with Warehouse and Procurement.
In Charge For all cranes:
Review/Produce Maintenance Plan as per Vendor recommendations
Review/Correct/Create corrected BOMs in SAP, establish MRP parameters
Ensure equipment are certified by third parties.
For all Hoist Winches:
Review/Produce actual Maintenance Plan
Review/Correct/Create corrected BOMs in SAP, establish MRP parameters
Ensure equipment are certified by third parties.
To assist sites with routine troubleshooting, local emergency procurements and repair optimization to reduce equipment downtime.
To assist Procurement Department with technical clarifications when required.
To coach and train junior engineers in all aspects related to the maintenance of cranes and lifting equipment
CONTEXT AND ENVIRONMENT
Deal closely with TotalEnergies EP Nigeria (TUPNI) field operations in maintenance, procurement, construction, projects,and logistics.
Externally to deal with Nigerian partners and equipment OEM.
FPSOs are located offshore (40 KM) and Onshore.
Striving to achieve cost saving and best value for money in Cranes and Lifting Equipment maintenance activities.
Progress competency level of staff working in Cranes and Lifting Equipment section.
Closely monitor developments in relevant local and international business environment
Accountabilities
Within the framework of DW Field Operations (AKPO-EGINA), the main objectives are, in the field of Cranes and lifting equipment, to:
To ensure all engineering processes, inspection and maintenance are efficiently carried out in strict compliance with safety policies and procedures on all lifting equipment.
To ensure lifting support as technical authority to DW Field Operations efficiently and in accordance with Company Rules,
Statutory rules and regulation in order to assure the oil and gas production targets within the estimated budget.
To ensure the reliability and availability targets of DW lifting equipment are according to Company HSE standards.
To analyze mechanical maintenance activities and lifting equipment performance from the technical and economic perspective and takes the action necessary to achieve company set objectives regarding efficiency, cost optimization and savings.
HSE OBJECTIVES
Familiarize self with TUPNI emergency procedures, carry out assigned responsibilities safely and report any incident, unsafe act or operation. Demonstrate personal commitment to HSE policy.
Take appropriate action to close out Downgraded Situation (DGS) relating to cranes and lifting equipment including the useof SYNERGI to update status.
Develop derogation dossiers, HSE audits and participate in Root Cause Analysis (RCA) related to discipline.
Ensure that contractors mobilized to offshore locations comply with COMPANY standard with respect to procedures and HSE training requirements.
Maintain awareness of and ensure compliance with all relevant Statutory and Company HSE standards.
Ensure all personnel under his/her supervision are well trained and aware of their HSE responsibilities with continuous monitoring.
Qualifications / Experience Required
Formal education: B.SC. Mechanical Engineering (2.1).
Professional experience (number of years): 15 years’ experience with:
Technical knowledge and experience in Offshore cranes and hydraulic power transmission and control systems
Proven experience working with heavy machinery/equipment
Extensive experience within maintenance, fault finding, build and procurement of equipment projects
Team management, analytical and organizational skills.
Computer literacy and knowledge of Computerized Maintenance Management System (SAP) is an advantage.
Proficiency in English language.

About This Role
Job Title:
Chief Operating Officer (COO)
Industry:
Construction, Chemical Manufacturing & Distribution
Location:
Lagos
Employment Type:
Full-time, On - site
Salary Band:
₦1,000,000 - ₦1,500,000 Net
Job Summary
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operational functions of the construction firm, ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, safely, on time, within budget, and in line with regulatory and quality standards. The COO will translate the company’s strategic objectives into executable operational plans, optimize processes, manage project performance, and drive operational excellence across all construction sites and support functions.
Key Responsibilities
Lead construction operations, site management, procurement, logistics, and project delivery teams, ensuring smooth coordination across engineering, finance, HR, and supply chain.
Oversee planning and execution of multiple projects, monitoring KPIs, cost, and productivity, and resolving site or contractor issues promptly.
Develop and manage operational budgets with the CEO and Finance team, driving cost efficiency without compromising safety or quality.
Enforce health, safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance across all sites.
Drive process improvements and operational systems to boost productivity and reduce waste.
Lead, mentor, and develop senior managers and site leadership teams; manage relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and regulators.
Support the CEO on strategic initiatives, business expansion, bidding, and risk mitigation.
Qualifications & Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Quantity Surveying, or a related field.
A master’s degree (MBA, MSc) is an added advantage.
Minimum of 10–15 years progressive experience in the construction industry.
At least 4–6 years in a senior operational or leadership role (e.g., Operations Manager, Project Director, Deputy COO).

Job Title: UT Level 2 Technician – Pipe Mill
Location:
Lagos
Work Mode:
Full-Time | Onsite
Industry:
Steel & Mining Industry
Job Summary
The UT Level 2 Technician is responsible for performing, interpreting, and managing ultrasonic testing inspections on steel pipes during or after the manufacturing process. Working within a pipe mill environment, the successful candidate will operate both Automated Ultrasonic Testing (AUT) systems and manual equipment to detect internal, surface, and subsurface defects, ensuring all products comply with strict international pipeline standards (EN10893-11) before shipment.
Key Responsibilities
Inspection & Process Control
Monitor, set up, and operate Automated Ultrasonic Testing (AUT) systems integrated into the pipe production lines.
Perform manual UT scans to verify, map, and validate indications identified by automated production line scanners.
Calibrate UT equipment, transducers, and automated systems daily using specific pipe mill reference standards (notched or drilled calibration pipes).
Inspect pipe body, weld seams (SAW, LSAW, or FCAW), and pipe ends (bevels) for laminations, cracks, porosity, lack of fusion, and wall thickness variations.
Evaluation & Reporting
Evaluate inspection data against pipe manufacturing codes and customer specifications, including API 5L, ASTM, ASME, and ISO 3183.
Accept or reject pipes based on applicable code criteria and accurately mark defect locations for repair or crop stations.
Prepare and sign off on official UT inspection reports and enter quality data into the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) or ERP.
Leadership & Quality Assurance
Provide technical guidance and supervision to UT Level 1 operators and scanner attendants on the mill floor.
Support Quality Engineers during third-party customer audits and witness inspections conducted by agencies such as Lloyd's, DNV, or ABS.
Requirements
Certifications (Mandatory)
Valid UT Level 2 Certification in accordance with ISO 9712 (PCN/CSWIP).
Valid VT Level 2 Certification in accordance with ISO 9712 (PCN/CSWIP).
Must pass an annual vision examination (Jaeger 1 and Ishihara color blindness test).
Preferred Certification
Additional Level 2 certification in Magnetic Particle Testing (MT) for pipe end inspections.
Experience & Knowledge
Minimum of 2–3 years of experience in a pipe manufacturing mill or heavy steel tube manufacturing facility.
Strong experience inspecting heavy-wall longitudinal or helical submerged arc welds (SAW).
In-depth knowledge of API Spec 5L line pipe, EN10219 specifications, and related NDT standards, including ISO 10893.
Required Skills
Strong technical ability to troubleshoot mechanical and electronic issues on automated scanning systems.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment.
Proficiency in interpreting computerized UT data streams, strip charts, and digital imaging.
Working Conditions
Willingness to work shifts, including nights and weekends, to support continuous mill operations.
Comfortable working in a loud, dusty manufacturing environment with varying temperatures.
Strong commitment to workplace safety around overhead cranes, moving pipe conveyors, and automated machinery.

job_title: Health Sector Joint Annual Review (JAR) Consultant
description:
Consultant - Health Sector Joint Annual Review (JAR) 2026
Lafiya is the UK Government’s flagship health systems strengthening and reform programme in Nigeria, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and delivered by Palladium. Running from 2020 to 2028, it provides embedded technical assistance to federal, state and local institutions to accelerate sustainable reform and improve outcomes for Nigeria’s most vulnerable populations.
The programme operates at federal level, in the Federal Capital Territory, and across five priority states: Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Borno and Yobe. It supports 138 Local Government Areas and has three overarching objectives: to catalyze Nigeria’s political and financial commitment to health, especially for the poorest; strengthen upstream systems for basic health and nutrition services; and increase uptake of modern contraceptives among women of reproductive age.
Lafiya’s Defining Feature Is Its Politically Informed, Embedded Approach, Which Translates National Policy Into Effective State-level Implementation. It Is Aligned With Government Priorities, Including The Health Sector Wide Approach, Annual Operational Plans, Budgets And The HOPE PHC Reform Agenda, And Works With Financing Mechanisms Such As HOPE PHC And BHCPF 2.0 To Unlock Sustainable Health Financing At Scale. The Programme Scope From April 2026 To September 2028 Is Organized Around Five Output Areas
Output 1:
Strengthened governance to improve coverage and delivery of integrated health services
Output 2:
Strengthened health financing, including through DRM, improving efficiency, increasing financial protection, and by leveraging financing at scale
Output 3:
Support to address human resources bottlenecks including health workforce migration
Output 4:
Strengthened health information systems, including using data for decision making, and harnessing digital health
Output 5:
Improved availability and sustainability of quality health commodities, including family planning
Cross cutting priorities, SRHR, nutrition, health security, climate adaptation, and resilience are integrated throughout, ensuring reforms deliver inclusive and sustainable health outcomes.
The Joint Annual Review (JAR) serves as a standardized accountability platform that brings together stakeholders in the Nigerian health sector to evaluate program performance, assess resource mobilization, distribution and utilization, and review health outcomes. Conducted within the Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp) framework and the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, Research and Learning (MEARL) Plan, the JAR ensures alignment with national health priorities, including the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII) and the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint (HSSB) 2023–2026. It fosters multi-stakeholder coordination and sets performance-based priorities for the subsequent fiscal year, closely linked with the national budgeting cycle.
The 2024/25 JAR meetings have been convened since the launch of the NHSRII and the signing of the Health Compact. It operationalized the "One Report, One Conversation" principle under SWAp and was led by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (FMOHSW) in collaboration with states, agencies, development partners, and other stakeholders.
To ensure a much more effective JAR meeting, and course-correction as we implement the Nigeria Health Sector, Renewal and Investment Initiative (NHSRII), the Minister conducts quarterly dialogues with State Commissioners of Health, and quarterly ministerial oversight committee meetings (now expanded beyond the BHCPF), and submits quarterly reports to Mr. President on signed Ministerial performance bonds. The quarterly review of all LGA and State AOPs, and reports of all TWGs contribute to discuss during the meetings above and form the basis for the JAR and the State of Health of the Nation Report SOHNR.
However, the officers of the Ministry responsible for the development of the SOHNR struggle with the process due to the late submission of data, limited ability for data clean-up and the inferential analysis required, as well as the multiple layers of proof-reading. As such, previous reports that have been produced (2024 and 2025 SOHNRs, and the 2025 JAR (Annual Statistics) Book, have been with incomplete data and errors.
Location:
the consultant will be based in Abuja
Total Level of Effort (LoE) Days
: 30 Days
Primary Duties And Responsibilities
Objective of the Consultancy
The Aim For The Engagement Of a Consultant Is To Ensure That The Necessary TA Support For The Development Of Critical Reports Such As The 2026 JAR (Annual Statistics Book; And The 2026 SOHNR. Specifically, The Consultant Will
Track progress on the resolutions from the 2025 Sector-wide JAR.
Track quarterly reports from MoC, Ministerial Performance Bonds, AOP reviews, State JARs etc
Undertake data clean-up and further analysis regarding the production of the 2026 JAR (Annual Statistics Book; and the 2026 SOHN reports;
Support/facilitate reporting writing workshops and validation meetings;
Undertake 1st and 2nd level of proof-reading of all reports produced.
Deliverables
The activities below are organized by component.
The TA Support Is Expected To Produce
The 2026 JAR (Annual Health Statistics Book) with revised indicators
The 2026 State of Health of the Nation Report
Specific Activity
Compile, analyze, and validate national health statistics data from relevant sources for the 2026 reporting year
Drafting, reviewing, validating, and finalizing the 2026 State of Health of the Nation Report, including trend and performance analysis
Expected Outputs
The 2026 JAR (Annual Health Statistics Book)
The 2026 State of Health of the Nation Report
Required Qualifications
An advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Demography, Health Economics, Monitoring and Evaluation, Health Informatics, Statistics, Health Policy, or a related field.
Relevant professional experience in health systems strengthening, health sector performance assessment, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, or public health research.
Demonstrated experience in the development, review, and analysis of national or sub-national health sector reports, annual reviews, scorecards, or similar health-sector performance publications.
Proven experience in data management, cleaning, validation, and analysis using large-scale routine health information systems and survey datasets.
Experience supporting Ministries of Health, government institutions, development partners, and donor-funded health programmes in Nigeria or similar settings.
Strong understanding of the Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp), health sector planning processes, joint annual reviews, and performance monitoring frameworks.
Familiarity with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII), Health Sector Strategic Blueprint (HSSB), and national health information systems will be an added advantage.
Strong analytical skills with demonstrated ability to interpret complex health data and produce evidence-based reports and recommendations.
Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools such as Excel, SPSS, STATA, R, Power BI, Tableau, or similar software.
Excellent report writing, editing, proofreading, and technical documentation skills.
Ability to synthesize data from multiple sources and present findings in a clear and policy-relevant manner.
Experience facilitating technical writing workshops, stakeholder consultations, and report validation meetings

description:
Locations:
Accra, Ghana
Lagos, Nigeria
Job Context
Lead the public health regional business development ambitions, by engaging MOH’s, funders, donors and related stakeholders to develop relationships, understand ways of working, and secure advanced knowledge of health-related procurement and supply chain related opportunities for DP World in the region. This role will drive the growth of DP World’s public health revenues in African markets by developing and executing a robust engagement strategy in the region.
DP World is expanding its healthcare and pharmaceutical capabilities to support access to affordable, high-quality medical products in the public health sector across Africa. This role is central to developing an understanding of the Ministry of Health, Central Medical Stores and public health supply chains in the markets within the region, with an ultimate view to gaining healthcare supply related business opportunities to increase the revenue and profitability for the DP World business units operating in the public health environment in Africa.
The Public Health BD Lead will operate at the intersection of customer relationship and account management, revenue generation, business operations and market expansion, in multiple markets in Africa. The role requires an understanding and appreciation of public health systems and Ministry of Health ways of working, with an ability to engage stakeholders at multiple levels within governments health infrastructures, and DP World hierarchy. The successful candidate will be instrumental in enabling DP World to partner with African Ministries of Health and Funders/Donors operating across the continent to secure revenue opportunities across the supply chain, prioritizing sourcing and procurement.
Key performance areas:
Business Development & Partner Onboarding
Meet and exceed sales revenue targets in public health across the African region.
Develop and maintain a pipeline of customer opportunities across the therapeutic areas including essential medicines, devices & equipment, and consumables.
Negotiate commercial terms, tender agreements, and partnership frameworks with various customers, partners and funders within the public health sector.
Identify, evaluate, and onboard local African distribution partners aligned with DP World’s in-country and above-country distribution businesses in public, humanitarian aid and private healthcare sectors.
Conduct due diligence and capability assessments of potential partners.
Strategic Market Expansion
Work closely with DP World’s Humanitarian Aid and Market Access teams in Africa to match tenders and emergency healthcare needs with business capabilities.
Identify opportunities for portfolio expansion (incl. Imres branded products) based on market intelligence and customer needs in Africa.
Gather and share market intelligence for the region of responsibility.
Identify and develop RFIs, RFQs, RFPs in conjunction with the Tender Lead for opportunities in PH.
Cross-functional Collaboration
Liaise with private market healthcare, freight, logistics, warehousing, and regulatory teams to ensure seamless supply chain execution.
Coordinate with finance and legal teams to manage contracts, payment terms, and risk mitigation.
Provide regular updates to leadership on customer performance, market trends, and BD progress.
Identify cross-functional opportunities and pass these on to the relevant BD person or capability.
Collaborate with other BD leads in other regions in Africa on joint opportunities that may span more than one area.
Performance Monitoring & Reporting
Track KPIs related to order inflow generation, sales revenue, margins, customer and partner onboarding, pipeline, trends, and market penetration.
Maintain dashboards and reports to monitor progress against strategic objectives.
Qualifications required:
Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in pharmaceutical or healthcare industry (minimum 3 years in the public health sector) with focus on sales, distribution and business development in multiple African markets and specifically in the region of interest.
An understanding of public health systems and government public health processes.
Proven track record in customer relationship management negotiations, and business development.
Experience in healthcare agent identification, partnering, contracting, due diligence and capability assessments are essential.
Experience in global healthcare supply chains is a plus.
Skills and Experience required:
Proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships with government stakeholders, partner agents' distributors, regulators, and internal stakeholders. Skilled in managing cross-cultural and cross-functional collaborations.
Understanding of business operations, industry dynamics, and key drivers of financial performance. Ability to translate financial data into actionable insights for non-financial stakeholders.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines. Flexibility to adapt to changing business needs and priorities.
Ability to analyze complex financial data, identify trends, and draw meaningful conclusions. Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
Capable of developing and executing long-term strategies that align with business goals, market dynamics, and customer needs across multiple geographies.
Familiarity with pharmaceutical regulations, WHO GMP standards, and African regulatory frameworks. Ability to navigate complex compliance and procurement environments.
Advanced MS Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel and Word skills required.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, timelines, and stakeholders simultaneously. Experience in leading customer onboarding and market entry initiatives.
About DP World
Trade is the lifeblood of the global economy, creating opportunities and improving the quality of life for people around the world. DP World exists to make the world’s trade flow better, changing what’s possible for the customers and communities we serve globally.
With a dedicated, diverse and professional team of more than 111,000 employees from 159 nationalities, spanning 77 countries on six continents, DP World is pushing trade further and faster towards a seamless supply chain that’s fit for the future.
We’re rapidly transforming and integrating our businesses -- Ports and Terminals, Marine Services, Logistics and Technology – and uniting our global infrastructure with local expertise to create stronger, more efficient end-to-end supply chain solutions that can change the way the world trades.
What's more, we're reshaping the future by investing in innovation. From intelligent delivery systems to automated warehouse stacking, we’re at the cutting edge of disruptive technology, pushing the sector towards better ways to trade, minimising disruptions from the factory floor to the customer’s door.
DP World is on a mission to transcend boundaries and bridge the gap between all nations and cultures – not just in what we do but also in how we behave.
We are dedicated to creating a culture where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to reach their full potential. We believe that embracing inclusion and diversity, drives innovation and growth and helps us connect people, businesses, and societies. Free minds and different perspectives are changing our world, and together we can change what’s possible.
WE MAKE TRADE FLOW TO CHANGE WHAT'S POSSIBLE FOR EVERYONE.

Job Title: Business Control and Inventory Manager
Location: Lagos Mainland
Employment Type: Full-Time
Industry: FMCG
Job Summary: - The role is responsible for providing oversight of the company's inventory, supply chain, procurement, finance and operational control. It ensures the accuracy and integration of inventory records, identifies operational risks and control weaknesses, investigates variances, and drives corrective actions to safeguard company assets, strengthen internal controls, and improve operational efficiency across the organization.
Key Responsibilities
§ Maintain oversight of inventory across all warehouses, Experience Centres and other stock-holding locations.
§ Ensure physical stock consistently reconciles with ERP/system, warehouse and Finance records.
§ Conduct scheduled and unannounced stock counts and investigate all material variances.
§ Review goods received, releases, transfers, returns, damages, shortages and inventory adjustments.
§ Ensure proper SKU-level tracking and prevent unauthorized movement or release of stock.
§ Review inventory ageing and identify slow-moving, non-moving and potentially obsolete stock.

Company Description
Skyway Aviation Handling Company PLC (SAHCO) is a publicly listed aviation ground handling services provider operating under the Nigerian Companies and Allied Matters Act of 1990. Originating from the former Nigeria Airways Limited and now part of the Sifax Group, SAHCO has a strong legacy in supporting the aviation sector in Nigeria. The company is listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange and is focused on efficient, safe, and rapid service delivery for airline partners. SAHCO is RA3 and ISAGO certified and consistently invests in personnel development, modern equipment, fleet renewal, and infrastructural upgrades. Its operations cover all activities from aircraft touchdown to takeoff, ensuring high-quality, compliant ground handling services.
Role Description
The roles at SAHCO is a full-time, on-site position based in Nigeria. This role is responsible for designing, reviewing, and optimizing mechanical systems and ground support equipment used in aviation handling operations. Daily activities include conducting technical assessments, overseeing maintenance programs, troubleshooting mechanical issues, and ensuring that equipment performance meets safety and regulatory standards. The Senior Mechanical Engineer collaborates with operations, procurement, and safety teams to plan upgrades, manage engineering projects, and implement continuous improvement initiatives. The role also involves guiding junior engineers and technicians, preparing technical reports, and supporting strategic decisions related to fleet replacement and infrastructural development.
Requirements:
• B.Eng in Mechanical/Electrical Engineering
• Minimum of 15 years' proven hands-on field experience
• Experience in Aviation, Oil & Gas, Construction, or Manufacturing.
Interested and qualified candidates are encouraged to send their CVs to humanresources@sahcoplc.com

who can pair deep test automation skills with generative AI tools — Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI API — to redefine how a modern engineering organization ships with confidence.

Job Description
About the Role
Our client, a prominent commercial bank with a strong presence in Yola, Adamawa , is seeking an experienced Senior Trade Finance Specialist. This crucial role involves managing and growing the bank's trade finance portfolio, providing expert advice to clients on international trade transactions, and ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations. The Senior Trade Finance Specialist will be responsible for structuring trade finance solutions, assessing risks associated with international trade, and building strong relationships with corporate clients engaged in import and export activities. The ideal candidate will possess extensive knowledge of trade finance instruments, international trade law, and risk management practices. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to the growth of international trade finance for our client in Yola, Adamawa .
Key Responsibilities Develop, structure, and manage a diverse range of trade finance products, including Letters of Credit (LCs), Guarantees, Documentary Collections, and Supply Chain Finance. Provide expert advice and solutions to corporate clients on their international trade financing needs. Assess and manage the risks associated with trade finance transactions, ensuring compliance with bank policies and international standards (e.g., UCP 600, ISBP). Build and maintain strong relationships with existing and potential clients, identifying opportunities to deepen engagement. Collaborate with relationship managers and other internal departments to provide integrated financial solutions. Monitor market trends and regulatory changes affecting international trade and trade finance. Ensure efficient processing and settlement of trade finance transactions. Conduct due diligence and assess the creditworthiness of clients involved in trade finance. Assist in developing and delivering training on trade finance products and services. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, International Business, or a related field. Professional qualifications like CDCS (Certified Documentary Credit Specialist) are highly desirable. Minimum of 6 years of experience in trade finance, international banking, or a related role. In-depth knowledge of trade finance instruments, international trade practices, and relevant regulations. Proven experience in managing client relationships and structuring complex trade finance solutions. Strong understanding of risk assessment and mitigation in international trade. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and negotiation skills. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport with clients and stakeholders. Proficiency in relevant banking systems and Microsoft Office Suite. Benefits
Our client offers a competitive salary and benefits package, including comprehensive health insurance, retirement savings plans, and performance-based bonuses. Opportunities for professional development and career advancement in the specialized field of trade finance are provided. Employees work in a dynamic environment in Yola, Adamawa , contributing to the facilitation of international commerce and enjoying a supportive team culture.

Basic Views
Human Capital Development Policy
In accordance with the Global HRM Policy, the Group has declared that, in order to accelerate the securing and promotion of global human capital, the Group will work to establish an environment in which employees can experience growth and self-improvement through their work, provide career opportunities regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, age, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, or disability, and develop global leaders, as the basic policy for human capital development.
Structures and Systems
SEI University
As part of its human capital development efforts, the Group provides training to help employees understand and share its corporate principles, values, and culture, as well as training aimed at improving their abilities, techniques, skills, and knowledge required to execute business strategies. The human capital development system composed of these training programs is collectively referred to as “SEI University.”
To achieve both the growth of each employee and the achievement of company targets, SEI University underpins “strong motivation for self-development” and “on-the-job training through guidance and dialogue with supervisors” as the basis for employee development.
■Global Common Knowledge and Skills
The Group has organized and integrated the training content and know-how cultivated since the establishment of SEI University and has established the Global Common Knowledge and Skills (GCK), consisting of knowledge and skills that employees should acquire according to their respective positions. While the basic knowledge is what employees should understand, the practical knowledge comprises knowledge and skills that are desirable for employees to acquire as basic abilities for performing their jobs. The Group is working to establish an environment where employees can take training at any time according to their own circumstances.
■Improvement of the training environment
To make it easier for employees active in over 40 countries and regions around the world to take training, the Group is spreading the use of the global learning management system “SEG e-CAMPUS,” in addition to the existing system that has been used mainly in Japan. SEG e-CAMPUS supports the languages of major bases, allowing for smooth streaming of e-learning programs and providing a wide range of content.
Starting with the launch in the Americas and Southeast Asia/Australia (APAC) in October 2024, the system had been spread to cover 11 countries and regions by the end of fiscal 2024. In fiscal 2025, the Group plans to further spread the system to cover a total of 22 countries and regions, including the previous year’s figure, by the end of fiscal 2025.
■Training program
SEI University offers over 400 training programs (shared globally) for all Group employees, from executives to new recruits, including compulsory courses for each level. Moreover, the Group provides company-specific training (specialized knowledge) to help employees acquire the specific knowledge and skills required by each business division or Group company.
Furthermore, the Group has introduced many practical training programs, including practical training for tackling manufacturing challenges and executive training in which cross-departmental teams are formed to propose solutions to actual management challenges.
Each curriculum is updated annually based on management challenges and other situations.

Initiatives and Results
Ba­sic train­ing pro­grams
Scene of the Sumitomo Spirit training
■ Spread of the Sumitomo Spirit
In the training provided by SEI University, the Sumitomo Spirit is positioned as the foundation for employees to carry out their work. The Group provides opportunities to learn about the Sumitomo Spirit at training programs for new employees and various level-specific training programs. In addition, the Group regularly communicates how a legal compliance program, a human rights program, etc. relate to the Sumitomo Spirit. Moreover, the President himself sends a message by video every six months, urging all employees to perform their duties in accordance with the Sumitomo Spirit. The video is translated into multiple languages and distributed to Group companies both in Japan and overseas. Furthermore, the Group provides advance training to employees who are to be assigned overseas so that they can communicate the Sumitomo Spirit in their own words in their new places of work. Additionally, the Group is training in-house instructors at Group companies both in Japan and overseas so that employees can regularly learn about the Sumitomo Spirit.
In 2023, the Group opened the Minami Hakone Gallery, a history exhibition room, in the Minami-Hakone Seminar House, one of its training facilities, so that visitors can experience the Group’s spirit, principles, values and culture. The training facility users can receive training from a full-time instructor regarding the Sumitomo Spirit and the history of Sumitomo. (In fiscal 2024, a cumulative total of 1,219 group employees took the training.) To achieve 2030 VISION and the Mid-term Management Plan 2025, both formulated based on the Sumitomo Spirit, the Group utilizes training, videos and other communication means to ensure that each employee regards the vision as their own issue and create job satisfaction.
Skills train­ing pro­grams
■DX
Defining the human capital necessary to promote the Company-Wide DX Plan as DX talent, the Group is strengthening the development of “core DX talent,” who can solve departmental challenges through initiatives that utilize digital technology, and “data analysis talent,” who understand data visualization and analysis methods and can apply them under guidance.
Manufacturing Human Capital Development Base Technical Training Center
■Manufacturing
Aiming to pass on the excellent technology and skills that the Group has cultivated and to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, the Group provides three types of training programs: basic manufacturing training, technical and skills training, and key-person training.
Basic manufacturing training（training seminar for new engineers）
Technical and skills training（Basic Mechatronics Training）
Key-person training（the Genba (on-site) Kaizen (improvement) Professional (GKP)）
Basic Manufacturing Training
The Group provides training to acquire the knowledge required at manufacturing sites, such as on safety and quality, as well as to learn about management techniques related to manufacturing. The Group provides not only curriculums for less experienced employees, but also regular training for employees at all levels, encouraging employees to reconfirm their basic knowledge and sharing information on the latest trends within the Group and on legal regulations.
Technical And Skills Training
Based on the principle of hands-on learning using actual machines and objects, the Group offers a variety of curricula that incorporate everything from the acquisition of the Group’s unique techniques and skills, including its equipment and maintenance techniques, to cutting-edge technologies such as IoT and AI. For the basic knowledge of improvement activities and equipment maintenance, the Group provides training overseas as well, primarily in China and Southeast Asia.
Key-person Training
The Group provides training for general managers in which general managers from Sumitomo Electric and presidents from affiliates confirm the concepts essential for reinforcing the manufacturing capabilities from the perspective of safety, the environment, quality, manufacturing and HR development and show their own commitment to proceeding with necessary activities. The Group also offers a plant manager development program to foster “strong” plant managers (equivalent to the manager of a manufacturing section) who will play a pivotal role in manufacturing. In addition, to develop the next generation of key persons, the Group offers practical training programs called the Monozukuri (manufacturing) Kakushin (innovation) Professional (MKP) and the Genba (on-site) Kaizen (improvement) Professional (GKP). In these programs, participants are assigned to theme departments other than their own and work there to solve the departments’ important challenges and problems for several months.
Man­age­ment pro­grams
SEG Management Program based on the Sumitomo Spirit (MPSS）（APAC）
■Management Program based on the Sumitomo Spirit (MPSS)
The Group annually provides training on the Sumitomo Spirit and management skills (SEG Management Program based on the Sumitomo Spirit: MPSS) for managers of Sumitomo Electric and Group companies at its bases in Germany, the U.S., Singapore, China (Shanghai and Shenzhen), Mexico, and Japan.
At the final reporting session of a GLP
■Global Leadership Development Program (GLP)
The Global Leadership Development Program (GLP), designed for general managers of Sumitomo Electric and Group companies, consists of online seminars and face-to-face seminars in Japan to help participants understand Sumitomo’s history and the Sumitomo Spirit, develop leadership skills, and build global networks.
Ex­ec­u­tive pro­gram
Participants climbing Mt. Besshi, the foundation of Sumitomo's development
■Executive training program
For executives of Sumitomo Electric and Group companies, the Group organizes workshops and other events so that they can try action learning, understand the Sumitomo Spirit, acquire management knowledge, and learn about leadership.
Total Hours of Training Programs
As a result of the efforts in each region and by each company, the accurate compilation of records by each company regarding its employees’ participation in training programs, and the development of a global learning platform, the Group achieved the global target of 20.0 hours / annually per headcount of training programs set in the Mid-term Management Plan 2025, before 2025.
To continue to provide training opportunities centered on the Global Common Knowledge and Skills (GCK), covering the Sumitomo Spirit, the Group will further improve the learning environment and offer content in multiple languages.
Ca­reer Di­a­logue
For each employee to grow, it is necessary for them to draw their own career vision based on their values and motivation regarding career and to actively work on self-development to realize that vision. At the same time, it is necessary for them to utilize the skills they have developed through on-the-job training to take on more challenging work. In this regard, the Group provides support for them to do so. Specifically, the Group provides training for managers regarding how to conduct career dialogue, as well as career training tailored to each employee’s position and age for those who have reached milestones such as their fifth year with the company, or turning the age 45 or 55.
The Group also ensures that career counseling is provided by in-house career consultants to those who wish to receive it.
Re­in­force­ment of Group Col­lab­o­ra­tion and Global Re­sponse
■Expansion to Group companies in Japan
To realize group-wide promotion of human capital development, the Group provides Group companies in Japan with information about training programs hosted by Sumitomo Electric and invites them to participate, and also spreads the common learning management system to cover the companies, thereby increasing face-to-face training and e-learning opportunities. The number of employees of Group companies in Japan participating in training for new employees, training for newly promoted employees, training by level, and training for mid-career recruits is increasing every year. Moreover, if it is difficult for a Group company to run training on their own, Sumitomo Electric sends in-house instructors to provide the necessary training at the relevant company.
■Global expansion
The Group operates the aforementioned training programs for executives and managers as opportunities shared both in Japan and overseas. (In addition, to promote human capital development that meets local needs, the Group regularly calls human resource manager meetings in each country and region to plan and operate various training programs (mainly for non-managers). The Group also discusses human capital development challenges within the Group with members involved in human capital management and development in Japan and overseas and organizes global common training.
Furthermore, the Group began to spread the global learning management system SEG e-CAMPUS from the second half of fiscal 2024 to improve the e-learning environment. Going forward, the Group will continue to raise the bar for human capital development and strengthen governance by organizing face-to-face training sessions that enable direct communication and developing and providing global common online learning content that can be studied from anywhere.

**JOB CONTEXT**  

The Senior HR Business Partner (HRBP) operates in a dynamic, fast\-paced environment, serving as the critical link between HR strategy and business execution. This role navigates complex organizational structures, balancing corporate HR policies with the unique needs of assigned business units or functions.
  

**Key Responsibilities**  

**Strategic HR Leadership**  



* Partner with C\-suite and senior leaders to align HR strategies with business objectives, ensuring workforce plans support growth and transformation.
* Lead organizational design initiatives, including restructuring and change management programs.
* Develop and implement HR policies and programs that drive engagement, productivity, and a high\-performance culture.
* Partner with Finance, IT, and Legal to align HR processes with business needs (e.g., workforce planning, system integrations).
* Resolve operational conflicts (e.g. hiring freezes vs. talent needs) through data\-backed recommendations.
* Lead process change initiatives (e.g. new performance management system rollout) with clear communication and training.
* Act as the escalation point for complex HR inquiries, ensuring timely and accurate resolutions.
* Develop self\-service resources (FAQs, knowledge bases, chatbot support) to empower employees and reduce dependency on HR.
* Partner with leadership to enhance employee engagement through recognition programs, career pathing, and wellness initiatives.
* Analyse engagement survey results and co\-create action plans with business leaders to drive improvements.
* Advise leaders on people strategies that align with business goals (e.g., workforce planning, retention tactics).
* Provide data\-driven insights (e.g., attrition trends, skills gaps) to support decision\-making
* Train leaders on HR tools, policies, and best practices (e.g., performance coaching, conflict resolution).
* Develop manager playbooks (e.g., hiring guides, promotion criteria) to ensure consistency and fairness.
* Oversee end\-to\-end talent acquisition for critical roles, ensuring alignment with diversity and skillset requirements.
* Design succession planning frameworks and leadership development programs to build pipeline readiness.
* Analyze workforce trends (attrition, skills gaps) to forecast talent needs and recommend proactive solutions.
* Resolve complex employee relations issues (e.g., grievances, disciplinary actions) while mitigating legal risks.
* Ensure compliance with labor laws and industry regulations across all locations.
* Promote inclusive workplace practices, addressing bias, harassment, and equity concerns.
* Drive performance management cycles, coaching leaders on goal setting, feedback, and accountability.
* Partner with Compensation \& Benefits to design competitive pay structures, incentive plans, and retention strategies.
* Leverage HR analytics to assess program effectiveness (e.g., engagement surveys, turnover metrics).
* Identify training needs and curate L\&D initiatives (e.g., upskilling, mentorship programs) to close capability gaps.
* Facilitate leadership workshops and team\-building interventions to strengthen collaboration.
* Optimize HR processes (onboarding, exits, mobility) using digital tools
* Developing comprehensive strategic recruiting and retention plans to meet the human capital needs of strategic goals
* Developing and implementing comprehensive compensation and benefits plans that are competitive and cost\-effective for the firm
* Providing overall leadership and guidance to the HR function by overseeing talent acquisition, career development, succession planning, retention, training, leadership development, compensation, and benefits globally

* Act as a trusted advisor to managers, providing coaching on people management best practices.
* Collaborate with Centers of Excellence (COEs) like Talent Acquisition and Total Rewards to deliver seamless HR services.

FairMoney is a pioneering mobile banking institution specializing in extending credit to emerging markets. Established in 2017, the company currently operates primarily within Nigeria, and it has secured nearly €50 million in funding from renowned global investors, including Tiger Global, DST, and Flourish Ventures.


In alignment with its vision, FairMoney is actively constructing the foremost mobile banking platform and point\-of\-sale (POS) solution tailored for emerging markets. The journey began with the introduction of a digital microcredit application exclusively available on Android and iOS devices. Today, FairMoney has significantly expanded its range of services, encompassing a comprehensive suite of financial products, such as current accounts, savings accounts, debit cards, and state\-of\-the\-art POS solutions designed to meet the needs of both merchants and agents.


FairMoney thrives on its diverse workforce, bringing together talent from over 27 nationalities. This multicultural team drives the company's mission of reshaping financial services for underserved communities.To gain deeper insights into FairMoney's pivotal role in reshaping Africa's financial landscape, we invite you to watch informative video.  

  



**About the team**  



Payments Platforms owns the systems that move money at FairMoney — the rails, the ledger, and the integrations with banks and processors. Every disbursement, repayment and transfer runs through what this team builds, and it has to be correct whether it's midday Monday or 3am on a public holiday when a switch upstream starts timing out.  

  



**Requirements**  



* you have 5\+ years of experience and a track record of technical leadership
* you've worked in payments, banking or fintech, and you know how ledgers, settlement and reconciliation actually behave
* you have 2\+ years of experience with Go, Java, .NET or TypeScript
* you've built distributed, event\-driven systems and understand how they fail
* you're strong at API design and have integrated with external third parties at scale
* you have deep experience with relational databases — PostgreSQL or MySQL — including schema design, query optimisation, indexing and transactions
* you've worked with messaging and streaming systems like Kafka, RabbitMQ, SNS or SQS
* you've built and operated highly available, resilient, observable systems

you're a strong debugger — you're the person others come to when production is confusing  

* 

**What you'll be working on**  



We're hiring a Principal Engineer to help shape the technical direction of that platform.


We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies:


* Go for our services
* PostgreSQL and MySQL for persistent storage
* Kafka, RabbitMQ, SNS and SQS for asynchronous messaging
* Kubernetes and Docker to run our services

AWS for most of our infrastructure  
* 

**Responsibilities**  



* Direct integrations with banks, switches and payment processors across Nigeria
* Design, build and maintain the APIs and services that handle money movement at scale
* Contribute to the architecture of the payments platform — service boundaries, data ownership, and the guarantees we make
* Build for failure: idempotency, retries, reconciliation and settlement across systems we don't control
* Debug and resolve critical production issues across services and multiple levels of the stack
* Lead design reviews and set the standard for engineering quality across the team
* Mentor senior engineers and grow payments expertise in the org

Work closely with product, risk, operations and partner\-facing teams  
* 

**Benefits**  



* Private Health Insurance
* Pension Plan
* Training \& Development
* Remote work

Paid Time Off  
* 

**Recruitment Process**  



* HR Screening: 30 minutes
* Hiring Manager Interview: 30 minutes
* Technical interview with the Engineering team: 60 minutes

### **Job descriptions \& requirements**

  

  

**Debyl Limited** is an ISO certified EPIC company based in Port Harcourt and operating in the Nigeria Oil and Gas sector.

  

  

We are currently seeking a QHSE Officer**.** The Junior QHSE Officer supports the implementation and monitoring of Quality, Health, Safety, and Environmental (QHSE) policies across company operations. The role focuses on ensuring compliance with internal procedures, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices, while promoting a strong safety and quality culture within the organization.

  

  

**Key Responsibilities**


**Health \& Safety**


* Assist in implementing and enforcing workplace health and safety policies.
* Conduct routine site inspections and safety audits.
* Identify hazards, report unsafe conditions, and recommend corrective actions.
* Support accident, incident, and near\-miss reporting and investigations.
* Assist in safety inductions, toolbox talks, and safety trainings.

**Quality**


* Support quality control processes and inspections.
* Assist in monitoring compliance with quality standards and procedures.
* Help document non\-conformities and corrective actions.
* Maintain quality records and reports.

**Environment**


* Support environmental protection initiatives and waste management practices.
* Assist in monitoring environmental compliance and reporting.
* Promote environmentally responsible work practices.

**Documentation \& Compliance**


* Maintain QHSE documentation, registers, and records.
* Support ISO management systems (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001\) implementation.
* Assist in regulatory compliance and external audits.
* Prepare basic QHSE reports for management review.

**General Duties**


* Promote a positive QHSE culture across all departments.
* Support QHSE campaigns, drills, and awareness programs.
* Perform any other QHSE\-related duties as assigned.
  

  

**Qualifications \& Requirements**


**Education**


* HND / BSc in Environmental Science, Engineering, Safety Management, Industrial Chemistry, or a related field.
  

  

**Experience**


* 1–2 years experience in a QHSE or safety\-related role.
* NYSC completed
  

  

**Certifications (Advantageous)**

* Basic knowledge of HSE laws and regulations.
* Strong attention to detail and observation skills.
* Good report writing and documentation skills.
* Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to work under supervision and follow procedures.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  

  

**Personal Attributes**


* Safety\-conscious and proactive
* Organized and reliable
* Willingness to learn and grow in the QHSE field
* Team player with a positive attitude

Job Purpose
Unilever International (UI) is Unilever’s White Space Arm of Unilever - one of the fastest and most profitable business of Unilever.
UI works across the world to fill white spaces for Unilever. As intrapreneurs, we introduce Unilever’s brands into white space geographies like Korea, Pacific Islands, Mongolia, and spearhead launches of iconic household brands like Dove, Lifebuoy, Sunlight, Glow & Lovely, TRESemme into big markets like U.S, China, Western Europe, and SEAA.
As Unilever’s growth engine, we establish global white space businesses in key channels such as Health & Beauty, Discounters, E-Commerce, and alternate channels such as travel retail, marketing to institutional partners like the United Nations, and seeding Unilever brands to overseas diaspora who crave for a taste of their familiar home brands. Singapore is our global hub leading strategy, marketing thinking, seeding plans, and alignment with the global categories and supply chain. We have global presence and UI hubs all over the world.
SPEED is the mantra for our resounding success. To serve the underserved, we embrace a founder’s mentality, explore unchartered territories, redesign end-to-end business models to establish successful businesses. We make a difference by deeply caring for our consumers, customers and talents, focusing on that really matters, thinking ahead in time and working to win together.
Unilever International (UI) being part of Unilever is fully committed to ensuring that its products are fully compliant with local legislation globally and meet Unilever’s own high internal standards.
This position will play a critical role in ensuring we fulfill this commitment for all 4 business groups in Africa (East and west Africa - primary focus on Francophone Africa) in form product compliance, regulatory change management, all local product registration and certification. The role will report to Head of Regulatory Affairs 1UL Malaysia, UI Asia & Africa and will be part of larger 1UL RA team working closely with UI R&D and all the cross functional teams in UI. For regulatory advice and expertise, this role will work closely with the larger Unilever RA community as well as with external Regulatory Affairs Experts in all clusters.
UI Regulatory Affairs team leads this mandate and supports the entire Unilever International portfolio across the globe, dealing with a wide variety in compliance activities and interacts with across functions in Unilever. This role will manage regulatory & product compliance requirements for UI portfolio and innovation projects in Africa (East and West Africa) cross BGs. For regulatory advocacy and expertise, this role will work with Unilever Regulatory Affairs community as well as with external Regulatory Experts in all clusters.

Accountable for and the first point of contact for any regulatory requirement for UI business in East and West Africa and Francophone
Build UI RA expertise on local regulations across East and West African including Francophone continent across Home Care, Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care & Foods
Design and maintain process to support UI business in product compliance assurance
Builds & maintains a strong network of contacts in R&D, Marketing and Supply Chain to facilitate assurance of product compliance for Unilever International (UI)
Working with external experts and creation of an eco-system of RAP (Regulatory Affairs Partner i.e. regulatory consultants)

Strong ability to design processes and to land best practice
Strong Business acumen, agility & personal mastery.

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.
At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.
UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.
Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.
For every child, the right to a Future
How can you make a difference?
The core mission of UNICEF is to advance the rights of every child, regardless of location, in all aspects of its work—including programs, advocacy, and operations. The organization’s equity strategy focuses on the most marginalized and excluded children and families, putting children’s rights into tangible action. For UNICEF, equity ensures that all children have the chance to survive, grow, and achieve their full potential without facing discrimination, bias, or favoritism. Any child who faces an unequal opportunity in life—be it social, political, economic, civic, or cultural—experiences a violation of their rights. Increasing evidence shows that investing in the health, education, and protection of a society’s most disadvantaged members, and addressing inequality, helps all children realize their potential and contributes to the sustained growth and stability of nations.
Purpose of the assignment
Under the direct supervision of the Supply and Logistics Specialist, the Logistics Associate is responsible for supporting the continuous provision of affordable and high-quality supplies and services. This support is tailored to the specific context and is carried out in strict compliance with UNICEF’s policies, procedures, and ethical standards.
Summary Of Key Functions/Accountabilities
Clearance of incoming goods
In-country logistics
Support for warehouse and inventory management activities
Reporting
Planning
Liaise with Programme Section and Procurement Services Team to prepare all required import regulatory submissions to the appropriate agency.
Liaise with Programme Section and Procurement Services Team to ensure supply plan incorporate a distribution plan and required funding source.
Prepare in consultation with Supervisor estimate logistics commitments and allocation to vendors.
Monitor logistics spend and on a quarterly basis review adequacy of the outstanding logics commitments.
Clearance and Forwarding of Incoming Goods
Verify that all necessary documentation complies with export and import regulations.
Issue letters of Authority (LoA) in a timely manner to relevant state ministries, clearing agents, and customs or regulatory bodies before shipments arrive in the country.
Closely monitor the clearance process, promptly address any issues or queries, and ensure adherence to all customs regulations and tariffs.
Ensure the Unit’s monitoring tools are timely update to ensure accurate visibility of LoAs against the commitments raised to vendors.
In-Country Logistics
Initiate requests to select reliable freight forwarders or shipping companies from approved transport vendors for the movement of goods.
Coordinate with the selected carrier to arrange for timely pick-up and delivery of goods.
Track shipments in real time and proactively address any delays or issues that arise.
Confirm that all goods are delivered safely and on time to their intended destinations.
Support for Warehouse and Inventory Management Activities
Ensure all movement of goods is accurately recorded in Vision, in line with UNICEF guidelines.
Promote good warehouse management practices and ensure that third parties are trained accordingly.
Supervise the receipt and dispatch of consignments and supplies.
Prepare stock reports, monitor inventory to identify trends, and track inventory status from source to beneficiary.
Conduct regular physical inventory counts in the warehouses.
Prepare documentation for the disposal of commodities through the Property Survey Board committee.
Track supplies near expiration and ensure compliance with FIFO (First In, First Out) and FEFO (First Expired, First Out) approaches.
Reporting and Monitoring
Ensure all logistics movements of goods are reported according to UNICEF guidelines.
Monitor the performance of contractors to track Key Performance Indicators and identify any bottlenecks in logistics processes.
Maintain and develop further Unit’s monitoring tools to ensure real-time monitoring, tracking and regular reports to management and Programme Section of the status of UNICEF and PS shipments.

For every Child, you demonstrate...
UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

Builds and maintains partnerships
Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness
Drive to achieve results for impact
Innovates and embraces change

Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels.
UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status.
UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance.
UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially.
UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance.  Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments may also be subject to inoculation (vaccination) requirements, including against SARS-CoV-2 (Covid). Should you be selected for a position with UNICEF, you either must be inoculated as required or receive a medical exemption from the relevant department of the UN. Otherwise, the selection will be canceled.
Remarks
As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity.
UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable candidates are encouraged to apply.
Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason.
UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information.
UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reduction. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only).
The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member's original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force.
Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities.
Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category.
All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates.
