job_title: A Beginner's Guide to Tabular Editor 3: UI Customization & Code Assist Features
description:
Jan 25
Jan 25 A Beginner's Guide to Tabular Editor 3: UI Customization & Code Assist Features
Kurt Buhler
Data Modelling
Tabular Editor (TE) is a powerful, high-quality, external tool for Power BI & AS Tabular Models that helps you make better models more effectively. In the below article, I introduce how to navigate & customize the UI, as well as provide an overview of some key features that will boost your productivity.
This post is
part 3
of a weekly series about Tabular Editor (TE).
Part 2 about TE licenses is here.
Contents
Finding your way around Tabular Editor 3
Customizing the User Interface
3A. A reference of the file formats of Tabular Editor
3B. A reference of the Code Assist features in Tabular Editor
3C. A reference of the Windows of Tabular Editor
Finding your way around Tabular Editor 3
The first time you open
Tabular Editor 3
, you will see a default layout similar to the below.
A standard menu bar to select and modify the various properties and functions
A customizable icon toolbar for the main functionality
A customizable workspace consisting of rearrangeable windows for the many TE3 features
The default layout & toolbars in Tabular Editor 3
It’s a very clean, elegant layout, but there is a lot to unpack, especially if you are “migrating” from Tabular Editor 2. Below I give a whirlwind tour of the various features in Tabular Editor 3, briefly mentioning what they do and why they are useful.
Future articles will dive more in-depth to use-cases and tutorials of how to use these features.
So where can you find all these exciting new features? For example, how do you customize the user interface?
Customizing the UI in Tabular Editor 3
Customize the theme of Tabular Editor
Change the theme in Tabular Editor 3
Tabular editor has a lot of options to
personalize layouts and themes.
From the “Window” menu there are a lot of options to customize the UI in Tabular Editor. The first I’ll draw your attention to is at the bottom - changing the theme. I’m not sure how common this is, but the first thing I do with any application is try to change the appearance or theme to
Dark Mode
. Obviously! C’mon, gotta save your eyes. 👀
But actually, Tabular Editor 3 has a surprising amount of flexibility when it comes to customizing the theme. Personally, I prefer ‘Office Dark’, which you can select when choosing “Bezier” and adjusting the “Skin Palette”. There are a lot of options, though, so you can pick whatever works best for you, tweaking it a bit further, if you want.
In all of my tutorials and screenshots, I use the ‘Office Dark’ palette. Try a few of them for yourself and find one that works for you!
The many colours of Tabular Editor seen from the “Skin Palette” menu when selecting “Bezier” theme
Customizing window & toolbar layouts
Capture, save & re-use
window/toolbar layouts
The default layout of TE3 is quite similar to the one of TE2. However, unlike TE2, you can rearrange the windows however you like.
Not just sizes & dimensions, but also the position
, including making the
windows float
and repositioning them about your screen separately. You can also
close windows
you don’t frequently use or need, or
add ones that are hidden by default
. Once you find a layout you need, you can save and re-use it, later!
Don’t be overwhelmed! Rearrange elements to fit your needs
Why it’s useful: This is more than an aesthetic frill. Being able to rearrange your windows is not only important from an accessibility point-of-view, but also helps you set up a productive workspace in the tool. After you have been using TE3 for a few weeks, it’s recommended that you take some time to create & capture some layouts that help you be efficient. Some examples below:
Find & Replace window (hidden by default) to be always visible
Separate layouts for developing my own models vs. exploring / troubleshooting second-hand models made by other people.
Removing toolbar icons where I preferentially use keyboard shortcuts
Opening DAX Query or C# Script windows in a separate, floating window
Other customization options: toolbars, commands & options
From the
Tools
menu there are some other UI customization options for the toolbars. You can
add or remove tool icons
and groups of icons, or
make TE icons larger
for accessibility.
Other commands - for example saving window layouts - can be dragged into the toolbar
, as well. This can even be done with context-independent macros (i.e. that run over the entire model, all measures, etc.). For example, a macro that formats all DAX in your model can be added to the toolbar for ease-of-use!
So when it comes to customization and flexibility of the Tabular Editor 3 UI, it’s clear that there’s a lot to offer, here. It’s recommended that you spend some time on this, to create a layout that works for you.
Toolbar customization in Tabular Editor 3
You can add custom C# macros to the toolbar
Diving into the Main Menu
3A. A reference of save file formats in Tabular Editor
Opening & Saving Files / Models
Connect to your models
From the menu bar you may find the standard options & preferences. For example, the first thing you likely want to do is connect to or open an existing model. This is easily done from the small cube icon in the toolbar, or from the
File menu
, where you can also
open DAX / C# scripts
or models from the various save formats supported by Tabular Editor.
To connect to a
local
model, you need to either have the file in
a supported format
(like .bim, saved from TE2) or connect to a model local instance of Azure AS, which happens when you
open Power BI Desktop
on your machine.
For a
remote
model, you need to connect to a supported service. For Power BI, this only works with Premium capacities supporting XMLA endpoint connection (
Premium Capacity, Premium-Per User
).
Note the “Save to Folder…” option
File Menu & Save Formats
As Mentioned, From Here You Can Open Or Save Existing Models In Supported Formats, As Well As Scripts (C#, DAX & M) And Queries (DAX). The Supported Formats Are Detailed Below
TE Folder Structure
.bim format: Analysis services model metadata format. This is a semi-structured .json file describing the model, its objects, and their respective properties in a human-readable format. When saving your data model as a .bim file, you capture the overall structure of the model and object definitions, but save nothing
In the directory of the folder structure, you will also find the below:
database.json & TE Folder Structure: The preferred way of saving & working with your model, the TE folder structure serializes your model, separating & organizing the objects into distinct .json files and (sub) directories. This is very handy for source control, which I have written about here. The database.json file is a .json file containing TE settings information and descriptive information of the model, such as:
Basic info: Model name, guid & compatibility level (a 4-digit number describing the ‘version’ of the model)
Model annotations: For example, if auto date/time is enabled (__PBI_TimeIntelligenceEnabled) and the order of the Power Query queries.
When & how it was saved to the folder structure from Tabular Editor (and by which user)
Power Query groups* (folders), orders & names of queries therein.
NOTE that to my knowledge, Power Query folders (queryGroups) are not viewable or editable from the Tabular Editor UI of TE2 or TE3. Thus if you copy an expression from one model to another in TE, and that query is located in a query group, it will produce an error when attempting evaluation, which you can’t resolve from the TE UI itself, to my knowledge. You will need to edit this database.json to remove the query group before copying the query, or add it in to the new model’s definition.
Folders for each object group (i.e. tables, expressions) with each individual object therein as a .json file (i.e. a specific measure). Individual objects have their properties all inside the definition.
database.User.tmuo: If you are using TE3 in Workspace Mode (simultaneously connecting to the model both on desk & in the service), the .tmuo file will also be present. This file contains user settings and Workspace Mode information. The file is otherwise empty if there are no specific settings, or Workspace Mode is not used.
.pbit format: The Power BI template file format contains model metadata, allowing it to be loaded into Tabular Editor (unlike .pbix files). This is actually not supported by Microsoft, so it isn’t a recommended file format for working with your model. Note that this file format isn’t supported in TE3: Desktop.
.vpax format: This format saves the results and summary statistics of your model when analyzed by the VertiPaq Analyzer. This file is created by other tools integrated with VertiPaq Analyzer, i.e. to compare models before/after optimizations or to see how the model statistics have been evolving. It’s more an analytical format than a working format for your model.
Example of a database.json file
Now that you know how to navigate the TE3 UI and open & save your model in various formats, it’s time to take a look at the various features that will help you be more productive!
3B. Code Assist features
Find & Replace in Tabular Editor 3
Note the “
Find
…” & “
Replace
…”
Looking in the Edit menu
, we see the expected options for undo/redo and copy/paste, as well as the
Find/Replace option
, which lets you
search your model
, or
Find/Replace in open documents & expressions
. This can be a huge time saver when modifying existing code in repetitive ways. Note that - as mentioned above - the
Find/Replace window can be docked in the workspace layout
, so it’s easily accessible for searching your model.
Code Assist features in Tabular Editor 3
You’re probably noticing the menu for Code Assist. Herein you find
context-sensitive functionality to help author DAX code
(and M, C#, to a lesser extent). These options will be enabled when
using the Expression Editor or authoring DAX Queries
.
One of the biggest boons to productivity in Tabular Editor are these
plethora of code assist features for aiding DAX coding
. A few of these features (like commenting/uncommenting code) work also with M expressions and C# scripts. Below I give a brief overview of each of these features, how to use them and why they are valuable for your productivity.
Code Assist menu in ‘Edit > Code Assist…’
Peek Definition (Alt + F12):
“Peek Definition” - open a window-in-window to “peek” the definition of a measure (OTD% in this case)
When it can be used: When authoring DAX code, if your cursor is on a calculated object, or when right-clicking the object.
What it does: ‘Peek Definition’ for that object to check the underlying expression. This opens a “window-in-window” to view the code, which can be closed with ESC.
Why it’s helpful: When authoring complex expressions with inter-dependent / nested code, it’s needed to check what you’re referencing now-and-then. Peeking instead of opening a new expression window can - in the long-run - save a lot of time.
…Documentation (F12; ‘Go to Definition’):
When it can be used: When authoring DAX code, if your cursor is on a DAX function, or when right-clicking the function.
What it does: Navigates to a dax.guide webpage entry for it.
Why it’s helpful: Early on in your DAX journey, you will need to frequently check examples or documentation of functions to understand how to best use them or write code. For example, this is handy for checking quickly optional arguments or expected datatypes.
When it can be used (2): If you’re selecting a model object (i.e. a normal column or table) or right-clicking the object.
What it does: This will snap to the object in the TOM explorer, so you can check the properties or home table, for example.
Why it’s helpful: Like “Peek Definition”, complex expressions may require frequently checking other objects. You might need to check an object’s properties - Data Type or Format String, for example- or see if a table has security (RLS, OLS) rules active.
Define Measure (No Keyboard Shortcut)
Defines upstream the measure
When it can be used: When writing a DAX Query and the cursor is on a measure, or right-clicking the measure.
What it does: Defines the measure expression at the top of the query (similar to ‘Script DAX’). If you have used DAX Studio before, you will be familiar with this functionality.
Why it’s helpful: When debugging, testing and optimizing DAX code, defining the measure upstream of the query will let you make small changes without having to modify the measure object expression and save these changes to the database.
Inline Measure (No Keyboard Shortcut)
When it can be used: Same as Define Measure
What it does: Replaces the selected measure with its expression.
Replaces the [# Invoices] measure with it’s expression
Why it’s helpful: There are cases when iterating DAX code, one may with to use the underlying expression rather than a measure reference. This is because a measure always is wrapped in an implicit CALCULATE statement.
Format DAX (Long-line: F6; Short-line: Shift+F6):
When it can be used: When a DAX expression is in the primary window.
What it does: Formats the DAX code either with Long-Line formatting or Short Line formatting using daxformatter.com from sqlbi.
Why it’s helpful: If it’s not formatted, it’s not DAX. Formatted DAX code is essential to maintain readability & elegance of the code in your model. What’s even more powerful, you can leverage this functionality in C# scripts to format all objects at once. So, there’s no excuse to not format your DAX!
Comment/Uncomment Code (No Keyboard Shortcut)
When it can be used: When the cursor is in any expression editor or query window (including DAX, M, C#)
What it does: Comments out the line by inserting two forward slashes (//) or dashes (—), depending on the setting in the “Tools > Preferences…” menu. This deactivates the specific line. “Uncommenting” removes these inserted characters.
Why it’s helpful: Instead of deleting code, it’s often preferable to comment out lines or parts you want to remove. Then, if you want to add it back, you just have to “uncomment” the code. Additionally, it’s commonplace to use comments to document the steps in the code for other developers (and your future self). This is a good practice, both for governance as well as learning code (DAX, M, C#).
Refactor (CTRL + R):
Replacing or removing all DAX variables at once
When it can be used: When the cursor is on a DAX variable, or when right-clicking the variable.
What it does: Initiates a “Rename Variable” mode, where all variables with the same name change if you alter one of them. You have to press ESC to back out of this mode, and press ENTER to submit your changes if you just one to change or delete of the variables in the code, for example.
Why it’s helpful: An alternative to “Find/Replace”, this can be an elegant way to gain some extra time, efficiently replacing, removing or re-naming variables in a DAX expression.
Show Calltip (CTRL + SHIFT + SPACE):
Calltip for SUMX, when highlighted for the first argument
When it can be used: When the cursor is on or inside of a recognized DAX function (i.e. when the cursor is on a specific argument, or when right-clicking it).
What it does: Shows a summary of the required arguments of the function with a brief description, including key tags like ITERATOR or CONTEXT TRANSITION.
Why it’s helpful: This is extremely helpful - especially for DAX beginners - to understand the code. For example, what parts of the code are affecting your evaluation context, or to know where an iteration is occurring. This callout tooltip also appears when authoring code and is an extremely effective way to be informed on what a function is doing, and what is needed for it to work properly.
Autocomplete (CTRL + Space):
The Tabular Editor 3 Autocomplete menu
When it can be used: When typing an object from the model.
What it does: Brings up the Autocomplete menu, from which you can select an element to enter at the cursor’s current position using Tab or Enter.
Why it’s helpful: This is a matter of preference but can help you to type code faster, particularly when objects have long or ambiguous names (which is hopefully not the case 😉 )
3C. Overview Of Main Windows In Tabular Editor 3
Note the “Dependencies” & “Debug” windows
TE3 is stuffed-full of features. There’s a lot to unpack, that much is clear from the
code assist
section, alone.
View
: This reveals windows that are closed or not presently visible. The default view has all of these visible except for the Best Practice Analyzer, Dependencies, and Debug windows. Below I will just briefly summarize what each window shows/does, as I have written separate articles about each of them which I will be publishing in later weeks (from now: Jan 2022).
TOM Explorer:
One of the major reasons why Tabular Editor has become such a popular tool for developing Power BI data models, the TOM Explorer is an interactive, indented, tree-like view of the tabular object model (TOM). This gives a nice overview of what’s in your model, and is where you will be creating, modifying and organizing (in display folders) objects. Intuitively dragging & dropping objects from the TOM Explorer to other windows (or to other parts of the TOM Explorer) is also supported.
Why it’s helpful: This is the meat & potatoes of Tabular Editor. It’s such an elegant way to browse and interact with model objects, and supports simple UX features like drag & drop, or an extensive, context-dependent right-click menu.
Best Practice Analyzer (BPA):
A tool that uses rules to
automatically scan your model for violation
s, to enforce
standards
in the model and alert the user to any properties or expressions that may be violating best practice conventions. A common example are [Columns] not clarified with the ‘Table’ name before it.
Why it’s helpful: The Best Practice Analyzer is particularly handy if you are often exposed to models created or modified by others, and you need to save time in checking them for potential issues. If you invest time in setting good rules that work for you (there’s a good standard template to start with), you can be notified when inevitably making a mistake, or inadvertently making a model decision that goes against best practices.
Messages:
Where you are alerted to problems in the model (i.e. from the BPA) or authored code (DAX, or errors compiling C# scripts). Double-clicking the message will instantly navigate to the problem object.
Why it’s helpful: Since TE3 will automatically proof your DAX code, this is a fantastic time-saver for squashing bugs and finding issues.
Data Refresh:
The UI that shows
in-progress and completed asynchronous refreshes
; i.e. when you use Tabular Editor 3 to refresh or recalculate parts of the model (tables or partitions).
Why it’s helpful: If you need to refresh a single table or partition ad hoc, the Tabular Editor UI is definitely the most effective way to do this.
Refresh tables & partitions from Tabular Editor 3’s TOM Explorer
Expression Editor:
Where you edit DAX expressions for various TOM objects (measures, calculated columns, calculated tables, roles, detail row expressions, calculation items), as well as
edit M code
(for partitions loaded into the model and shared expressions like parameters, which aren’t).
Change M code outside Power BI - M code made in Power Query can be viewed & changed from Tabular Editor
Macros:
C# scripts that are saved for easy re-use from the right-click context menu.
Why it’s useful: This is Pandora’s box - the C# scripts & macros in Tabular Editor 2 & 3 can really explode your productivity. You can create custom actions to
automate or streamline development tasks
, from basic things like formatting all the DAX in your model, to more complex operations.
VertiPaq Analyzer:
Integration of the VertiPaq analyzer tool, which can analyze and provide valuable summary statistics about the data model. The VertiPaq analyzer is also integrated in the DAX Studio external tool.
Why it’s useful: Collecting statistics on your model is an essential step prior to optimization. This will inform you about bloating objects in disk size as well as the cardinality size of relationships.
When troubleshooting a model, a first step should always be running the VertiPaq analyzer.
Dependency tree for a measure
Dependencies:
Reveals
dependency trees for model objects
(i.e. if a measure is dependent on 2 other measures, and a column). You can explore in both directions,
objects that depend on what you’re selecting
, and
what that object is dependent on
.
Why it’s useful: This makes it easy to explore models and
understand the upstream or downstream objects
for any given measure, for example.
Call Tree for a DAX measure in a query
Debug:
A recent acquisition to Tabular Editor version 3.2.0, Debug pertains to the new
DAX Debugger feature
of Tabular Editor 3. This allows you to investigate explicitly defined measures in your model using the
Pivot Grid
, or in
DAX queries
produced by SUMMARIZECOLUMNS (i.e. like the ones generated in Power BI, that can be copied & pasted from the Performance Analyzer).
Why it’s useful: This is a very valuable tool for a developer to write complex DAX code more effectively, and understand better what is happening in each step of the process. Using a
DAX Query
or
Pivot Grid
, you can
right-click a cell and ‘Debug’ the explicit measure result.
This will give you information about:
The Call Tree of the measure
The Evaluation Context of that cell
Local variables active in part of the code
On top of this, you can also experiment in the evaluation context to understand how other expressions would be evaluated. Using the watch window, you can enter other DAX expressions ad hoc, then evaluate them to see what the result would be. This helps you better understand the evaluation context and what is happening in DAX.
Starting a debug session from a Pivot Grid, using an explicitly defined measure
Find & Replace DAX in Power BI (works with M, C# also)
Find & Replace:
Mentioned already several times above, the Find & Replace window is opened from within the Edit menu. It can be docked in the layout.
Why it’s useful: A big time saver for making
consistent replacements in code
. Having Find and Replace in Power BI DAX makes it so you can replace single words, object references, or complex text that might be re-used. You can also
search across the entire model
for certain words, or
using RegEx
if you’re a god among us common folk.
Properties:
Last is the Properties window, which shows information about a particular TOM object in the model that is being selected. The properties in this section can be altered from the Tabular Editor UI, but recall that not all of the properties can be modified from Power BI Desktop.
Hopefully this has been a useful summary of various key features accessible from the basic Tabular Editor UI. Future articles will go further in-depth about specific features, how to most effectively use them, and exploring a few business (data) use-cases.

- an overview of some key features in TE3
This post is
part 3
of a weekly series I’m writing about Tabular Editor.
Part 2 about TE licensing is here.
Next week, in
part 4,
we will dive deeper into the ‘meat & potatoes’ of Tabular Editor -
the TOM Explorer

Aakar Electrotech is on the lookout for talented individuals to join our team. We are a leading Industrial-grade Electronics Contract Manufacturer, and we are currently seeking individuals who are passionate about electronics manufacturing and eager to contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality electronic solutions to various industries.
LOCATION
New Delhi, India
EMPLOYMENT TYPE
Full-time
What You'll Do
At Aakar Electrotech, you will have the opportunity to work on cutting-edge electronics projects that cater to the specific needs of industries such as Automotive, Defense, and Education. You will be involved in the entire manufacturing lifecycle, from prototyping to production, and contribute to the development of innovative electronic solutions.
Our team is dedicated to pushing the boundaries of electronics manufacturing, and as a part of our team, you will have the chance to work on diverse projects and collaborate with experienced professionals in the field.

Crisis communication plans

Critical business functions
Recovery priorities
Recovery Time Objectives (RTO)
Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)
Operational dependencies

* You’ll be in the global Learning organisation, headed by VP Learning and part of the larger Talent \& Learning organisation.
* The Learning organisation comprises all the capabilities required to deliver the end\-to\-end learning lifecycle from identifying skill \& knowledge gaps to delivering a high impact learning \& KM experience.
* The purpose of Learning at Shell is to most effectively, efficiently, and with speed, build required and critical individual skills that contribute to building differentiated organizational capabilities and accelerate Shell’s achievement of Powering Progress Strategy.

* Improving the foundation: License\-to\-Operate Training

* Being a strategic partner to business: Building Differentiated Skills
* Enhancing the impact of learning: Strengthening Employee Value Proposition

Sustaining transformation: Empowering our Culture of Learning.

**Where you fit in**  



* The context we operate in is constantly evolving, with a growing demand for the energy that powers lives and communities.
* While the mix of energy sources is changing, oil and gas will play a crucial role for years to come.
* Through investment, innovation, and a value\-driven approach, our new Integrated Gas \& Upstream (IGU) business will continue to provide secure, increasingly lower\-carbon energy for a balanced transition.
* You’ll be part of the Deep Water (DW) Nigeria Learning team; whose purpose is twofold:
* Firstly, to protect value at the Asset and deliver against our table stakes by ensuring that Compliance and Competence Assurance processes run to expectations at Asset, as agreed with the local business stakeholders.
* Secondly, to create value at the Asset by understanding the local business needs, as part of the HR team, and leveraging the global learning solutions portfolios to deliver learning locally.

This will include formal Learning (e.g. courses, assessments, blended learning), informal Learning (e.g. Nuggets, Portals, external learning sources), and KM solutions to support learning in the flow of work.

* Partner with your Business \& HR stakeholders to understand the business priorities, skill gaps, learning \& Knowledge Mngt needs, create annual plan in alignment with broader DW Strategic Learning plan and prioritize value.
* Support and provide inputs to the DW Learning Manager on strategic learning \& KM needs for DW Nigeria
* Support ‘Foundational, Core to Compete and Differentiated’ Organizational Capabilities by leveraging the global learning portfolios in leadership, technical, commercial, and essential skills.
* Ensure delivery of the learning \& KM annual plan considering what is already internally available via the global learnings portfolio and/ or consider other options like buying market standard, bend existing learning \& KM solutions when designing impactful learning experiences (pulling on expertise and resources from broader Learning org)
* In limited situations, deliver upskilling/ courses yourself
* Driving together with the DW Nigeria business a workforce which can operate safely, compliant with local regulations and Shell global standards by giving advice on learning competence assurance options and ensuring that the Competence Compliance Assurance (CCA) processes run for your population to the levels agreed with local asset stakeholders. And aligned with the global Shell Learning CCA Governance.
* Understand the national, local and site regulations and standards affecting your population and ensure the right learning portfolio is available to them, working with learning operations and local partners to ensure delivery.
* In close collaboration with Nigeria HR, coordinate and manage the Nigeria Governmental Development fund and regular report status.
* Act as an active champion and role model on Learning Culture in the respective learner communities

You will ensure that the capability needs of your population, identified with the Business and HR team, are delivered and measured using leading and lagging indicators as much as possible, and fit for purpose.  
* 

**Key Skills**  



* You will bring relevant experience to the table, either as a Learning/OD/HR/ Talent professional where you can apply your skills to building capability in the subject area or as a technical/business professional where your network and knowledge can add value.
* The ability to work ‘cross boundaries’ and build up business knowledge or vice versa learning knowledge credibly and with speed will be critical
* If you are a Technical Professional, you will have a good network at the asset/function with knowledge of the asset/function activities. A willingness to learn about the profession of Learning is a must.
* If you are Learning Professional, alongside your professional expertise in Learning \& KM needs analysis, build/borrow/buy, curation, planning, change management, delivery and measurement, you must be willing to invest time to rapidly build domain knowledge and a network across the function or business.
* You will bring an outcome focus and ‘from the business back mindset to the role. You are comfortable in dealing with ambiguity and have a passion for integrating and collaborating across organisational boundaries. You challenge the status quo and drive for simplification.

You bring a Learner Mindset, a curiosity to learn and grow, learn from mistakes, successes, and speak up openly in a safe environment.

* Flexible working arrangements (including part\-time working) are supported where feasible, and are subject to applicable local policies, regulations and legislative frameworks.

If appropriate, please make clear in your application the type of flexible working arrangements you would like to be considered.

**An innovative place to work**  



* There’s never been a more exciting time to work at Shell. Everyone here is helping solve one of the biggest challenges facing the world today: bringing the benefits of energy to everyone on the planet, while managing the risks of climate change.
* Join us and you’ll add your talent and imagination to a business with the power to shape the future – whether by investing in renewables, exploring new ways to store energy or developing technology that helps the world to use energy more efficiently.

About Us
Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.
About The Role
Moniepoint is building innovation hubs at three of Nigeria’s leading universities: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). Each hub is a cross-disciplinary platform, open to students from every faculty. The model is cohort-based, industry-connected, and built to produce technical talent ready for the job market, across software engineering, AI, product, data science, robotics, and design. The hubs train students in applied technical skills, connect them to working engineers, product leaders, and founders, and provide a path into industry at Moniepoint, at other technology companies, or through ventures of their own.
This is a building role. The hubs are entering their operating phase, and you will own the design of how they run and the teams that run them.
What you will own
Programme design. You will design the operating model for all three hubs from the ground up: how cohorts are structured, how learning is sequenced, what “job market-ready” means at each level, and how graduates are assessed and certified. This is not adapting someone else’s playbook. It is writing one.
University relationships. You will be the primary relationship owner with the Vice-Chancellors, deans, faculty leads, and student bodies at OAU, UNN, and ABU. These are institutional relationships that require both strategic seniority and sustained presence.
Cross-faculty engagement. The hubs are not engineering faculty initiatives. They are open to students across every faculty: engineering, sciences, humanities, business, design. You will design the engagement model that brings students from across each university into the hub and keeps them in it through the full cohort.
Industry and mentorship pipeline. The hubs derive their value from the connection between classroom and industry. You will build and manage the network of engineers, product leaders, and founders, inside Moniepoint and beyond, who mentor, assess, and hire from the hubs.
Facilitators and standard. You will design the facilitator model, recruit the people who teach and assess, and own the standard those facilitators hold the cohort to. A single standard across all three hubs is non-negotiable; how it's delivered locally is yours to design.
Infrastructure and operations. You will own the physical footprint of each hub, whether that means a buildout from scratch or working within an existing campus structure, and manage the timelines, vendor relationships, and hub-level budgets across three sites. You will define the staffing model for each hub and recruit the on-ground team that runs them day to day.
Outcomes and accountability. You will set and own the metrics: graduate output, job placement, programme completion, cohort quality, employer satisfaction.
Pipeline integration. The hubs are upstream of Moniepoint Academy and other talent programmes. You will design the connective tissue between hub graduates and Moniepoint’s internal pathways, so the strongest talent has a clear next step.
Who you are
10+ years of experience overall, with at least 5 in leadership roles owning programmes, teams, and budgets end to end.
You have built or led a technical training or workforce development programme at scale, ideally across multiple sites. You have taken something from zero to one - designed the model, hired the team, and held the standard yourself.
You have held institutional relationships at senior level across universities, government bodies, and industry partners. You know how to navigate Nigerian university administration, or you have done it elsewhere and can credibly do it here. You have hired and managed technical educators, and you know what separates someone who can teach from someone who can teach to a standard.
You understand what good engineering education looks like and what employers in software, AI, product, and data science actually hire for. You don't need to write code, but you need the technical fluency to design a programme that produces hireable engineers, not credentialed graduates.
You are rigorous about outcomes and impatient with programmes that look good in announcements but cannot prove what they produce.
Experience in edtech, developer education, university-industry partnerships, or workforce development is a strong signal. Building something from scratch and owning it through to measurable outcomes is essential.
What success looks like
Year one. Operating model live across all three hubs. Cohorts running on a common standard. The facilitator team hired and held to the same expectations regardless of site. First graduate cohort exited, with a clear placement record into Moniepoint and into industry.
Year two. The hubs are recognised within Nigeria as the most credible cross-disciplinary technical training environment available to undergraduates. Employers, including Moniepoint, actively hire from the hubs. Cohort demand outstrips supply.
Year three. Hubs producing technical talent into Moniepoint at a cost-per-hire that justifies the investment, and into the wider industry at a scale and quality that defines what a corporate-funded university programme can look like in Nigeria. Model documented and ready to expand if leadership chooses.
What Moniepoint can offer you
The opportunity to shape one of the most consequential talent infrastructure investments in Nigerian technology.
A dynamic, diverse, and collaborative environment where every team member's voice is recognised and valued.
Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.
Competitive salary, individual performance bonuses, and firmwide performance bonus.
Company-covered health insurance plans. Pension plans.
What to expect in the hiring process
A preliminary conversation with one of our recruiters.
An interview with the hiring manager, our Head of Corporate Affairs.
A case study or written exercise on operating model design for the hubs.
An interview with our Group COO.
A final conversation with our CEO.

Our client is hiring a senior commercial leadership professional who will be responsible for driving profitable growth across a multi-channel retail business. The Buying & Merchandising Manager owns the full merchandise lifecycle, from seasonal assortment planning and buying, through in-season trading and inventory management, to markdown and end-of-season liquidation. The role sits at the center of a complex, fast-moving retail operation spanning Own Retail, Franchise, E-commerce, and Omnichannel channels.
This is not a support or coordination role. The person in this seat makes consequential commercial decisions daily, what to buy, how much to commit, when to push, when to mark down, and how to deploy inventory across channels to maximize sales and margin. They are equally responsible for the analytical infrastructure and team capability that makes those decisions defensible and repeatable.
The role reports to the Business Head and leads a team of three direct reports: a Planning Lead, a Buying Lead, and an Allocator.
What You Will Own
Buying, Assortment & Merchandise Planning
Lead end-to-end seasonal buying and merchandise planning across all channels and categories. This includes assortment architecture, range width planning, ABC grading, product selection, and big-bet initiative planning. You will drive Open-to-Buy (OTB) management, build demand forecasts grounded in historical performance and consumer trends, and own the Go-to-Market process from range planning through to product availability.
In-Season Trading
Own in-season trading performance across all channels. Monitor weekly and monthly sales, sell-through, and inventory data, identify risks and opportunities early, and recommend decisive corrective actions. You will co-own commercial review processes, track product launches and seasonal performance, and drive full-price sell-through as a primary commercial objective.
Allocation, Replenishment & Inventory Management
Lead allocation and replenishment strategies to maximize stock availability and eliminate stock-outs. Manage inventory deployment across stores, e-commerce, and omnichannel fulfillment points. Own cover weeks, size-level availability, stock transfers, and inventory balancing. Partner with Supply Chain to ensure timely merchandise flow and project inventory requirements through monthly sell-out tracking.
Omnichannel Merchandising
Drive inventory optimization across retail, franchise, and e-commerce simultaneously. Lead cross-functional initiatives that require coordination across merchandising, operations, and commercial teams. Support new store openings, dark store setups, and omnichannel fulfillment projects as the single accountable point of contact for critical merchandising decisions.
Markdown, Promotions & Commercial Planning
Develop and execute markdown and promotional strategies tied to brand guidelines and commercial targets. Plan and evaluate promotional calendars, manage End-of-Season and Mid-Season Sale execution, and lead inventory liquidation strategies that protect margin and brand equity while clearing terminal stock efficiently.
Analytics, Insights & Automation
Build and deliver merchandise analytics that drive strategic decisions, not just reporting. Use predictive analysis to sharpen buying accuracy and inventory productivity. Lead automation adoption across merchandising tools and systems, and champion best-in-class planning practices across the function.
Team & Stakeholder Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing buying, merchandising, and trading team. Set clear goals, drive accountability, and build succession depth. Collaborate closely with Supply Chain, Retail Operations, Franchise, E-commerce, Finance, Marketing, and Visual Merchandising teams to ensure aligned execution across the business.
How Performance Will Be Measured
Sales Growth, Gross Margin Achievement, Full Price Sell-Through (FPST), Inventory Turnover, OTB Adherence, Markdown Efficiency, Forecast Accuracy, Omnichannel Fulfillment Performance.
What We Are Looking For
8 to 12 years of experience in buying, merchandising, planning, trading, or retail inventory management, with demonstrated leadership of a team and ownership of commercial outcomes, not just contribution to them.
Sector experience in sportswear, fashion, lifestyle, footwear, or large-format retail is strongly preferred.
Candidates with structured retail or FMCG-adjacent backgrounds and strong inventory/planning depth will also be considered.
Strong working knowledge of omnichannel retail environments is essential. The candidate must understand how retail, franchise, and e-commerce inventory interact and be comfortable making decisions that cut across all three.
Advanced Excel and data analysis capability are baseline requirements. Experience with SAP is expected at this level.
Familiarity with demand planning tools such as O9, Increff, Blue Yonder, or equivalent systems is a significant advantage.
The ideal candidate is analytically sharp, commercially decisive, structured in their thinking, and credible enough to influence senior stakeholders across multiple functions.
A Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Marketing, Fashion Management, or a related field is required.

Job Title
: Oil & Gas Trader / Transaction Advisory Consultant
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Oil & Gas Trader to provide commercial and operational advisory support across oil and gas transactions. The successful candidate will support transaction monitoring, counterparty sourcing, risk assessment and the execution of petroleum product supply, import and export transactions.
This role requires strong industry relationships, practical transaction experience and a deep understanding of the operational, pricing, regulatory and geopolitical factors that affect oil and gas trading.
Key Responsibilities
Advise on the structuring, execution and monitoring of oil and gas transactions, particularly AGO supply and related petroleum products.
Review transaction documents, supply arrangements, logistics plans, pricing structures and payment terms to identify operational and commercial risks.
Monitor transactions from product sourcing and loading through transportation, delivery, discharge and settlement.
Provide guidance on vessel operations, including vessel nomination, chartering, documentation, inspection, loading, discharge and demurrage risks.
Support the verification and assessment of buyers, suppliers, traders, vessel operators, storage facilities and other transaction counterparties.
Introduce credible buyers, suppliers, traders, vessel owners, terminal operators and other relevant industry participants.
Advise on import and export processes, regulatory requirements, customs procedures, permits and associated documentation.
Provide timely intelligence on petroleum product pricing, supply availability, market movements and regional trading conditions.
Identify geopolitical, regulatory, operational, foreign exchange, logistics and pricing risks that may affect transactions.
Support transaction negotiations and provide practical recommendations based on previous industry experience.
Prepare concise transaction monitoring reports and escalate material risks or irregularities.
Requirements
Significant professional experience in oil and gas trading, petroleum product supply or downstream operations.
Demonstrable experience in AGO supply transactions.
Strong knowledge of vessel operations, petroleum product logistics, terminal operations and marine documentation.
Experience with the import and export of petroleum products.
Strong understanding of petroleum product pricing, margins, market benchmarks and transaction economics.
Existing relationships with credible buyers, suppliers, traders, vessel operators and other oil and gas industry participants.
Ability to assess counterparty credibility and identify fraudulent, commercially weak or operationally impractical transactions.
Strong understanding of regulatory, geopolitical, foreign exchange and supply chain risks affecting the oil and gas industry.
Excellent negotiation, communication, reporting and stakeholder management skills.
High integrity, sound commercial judgment and the ability to handle sensitive transaction information confidentially.
Preferred Profile
The ideal candidate is a seasoned oil and gas professional who has personally participated in the sourcing, negotiation, financing, transportation and delivery of petroleum products. They should be commercially connected, operationally knowledgeable and able to anticipate transaction risks before they result in financial losses.
Engagement and Compensation
This may be structured as a full-time, part-time or consulting engagement, depending on the candidate’s experience and availability. Compensation will be competitive and may include transaction-based performance incentives.

About Zipline
Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.
Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.
Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.
We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.
About You And The Role
Zipline is scaling nationwide medical delivery in Nigeria using long‑range autonomous aircraft. As the New Deployments Lead, Nigeria (senior individual contributor/people‑leader), you will own end-to-end delivery and launch readiness for Zipline sites so hospitals, clinics, and health systems reliably receive life‑saving products on schedule. You will operate at the nexus of construction, aviation regulation, supplier networks, and in‑country operations, translating Zipline’s global operational and safety standards into sites that are permitted, built, commissioned, and ready for flight operations. This role is high‑ownership and high‑intensity: you will be accountable for delivering the country deployment plan on schedule, within budget, and to measurable reliability and quality thresholds while building and leading the Nigeria deployments organization.
What You'll Do
Own full lifecycle delivery and formal operational handover for all new Zipline sites in Nigeria: site selection input, permitting and approvals, civil/electrical/communications construction, systems commissioning, safety acceptance, aviation clearance, and transfer to Operations.
Manage a portfolio of deployments (up to 12 total; concurrently up to 6 active sites), maintaining an integrated program plan with clear dependencies, critical paths, resource allocations, risk register, and escalation points.
Define, enforce, and report launch‑readiness acceptance criteria for each site as binary milestones plus percent‑complete against baseline (examples: permits approved, infrastructure to spec, power/comm uptime targets, systems commissioned, safety validations, aviation clearance). Drive acceptance tests and defect thresholds at handover.
Own program outcomes and tradeoffs: schedule adherence (plan vs. actual), budget variance (% and absolute), reliability/quality metrics at handover (defect rate, commissioning pass rate), and sites launched per quarter. Authorize corrective actions and rebalancing of scope/resources to protect safety, schedule, and budget.
Build, hire, and lead the Nigeria deployments team (project/program managers and site leads); directly manage external consultants, contractors, and on‑site supervisors during execution. Clarify reporting lines and decision authority with Country and Global Leadership.
Manage vendors and contractors end‑to‑end: scopes, contracts, schedules, costs, quality control, and on‑site supervision of civil, electrical, and communications work. Hold vendors to measurable acceptance tests and enforce remediation for defects.
Coordinate daily with Operations, Safety, Engineering, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and Country Leadership to resolve design, procurement, certification, and operational readiness issues that impact launch readiness.
Own in‑country deployment budgets and financial tracking; report variance explanations and corrective plans to country and global stakeholders.
Capture lessons learned and continuously improve Zipline’s deployment playbook, SOPs, commissioning checklists, and acceptance criteria to reduce defects and accelerate future launches.
What You'll Bring
8+ years of relevant experience in construction, infrastructure delivery, engineering, or technical program management, including at least 3 years leading teams or complex programs and demonstrable hands‑on field delivery experience.
Proven track record delivering multiple technically complex infrastructure projects concurrently through permitting, commissioning, and handover; experience in Nigeria strongly preferred.
Direct experience interacting with Nigerian regulatory bodies (aviation or infrastructure) and securing site permits/approvals for regulated projects.
Practical, demonstrable experience managing contractors and on‑site civil, electrical, and communications works and driving commissioning to measurable acceptance criteria and defect thresholds.
Strong program management discipline: integrated schedules, resource and contingency planning, budget ownership, risk register management, and decisiveness to make program tradeoffs.
Metrics‑driven: able to define, track, and report binary launch milestones, schedule variance, budget variance, and basic reliability/quality metrics at handover.
Comfortable operating in high‑intensity, ambiguous field environments with variable site conditions and supply‑chain constraints; able and willing to spend significant time on active sites.
Excellent stakeholder management and clear written and verbal communication with technical, regulatory, community, and executive partners.
Willingness and ability to travel frequently across Nigeria and be on‑site for extended deployment phases; must be based in or able to relocate to Nigeria for the role.
Legal authorization to work in Nigeria; Zipline may provide sponsorship where applicable.
Must be a licensed civil engineer.
What Else You Need To Know

It is ready when the people are trained, the systems are tested, the approvals are secured, and the operation can deliver safely and reliably from its first flight onward.
We are hiring an Operations Readiness Program Manager to lead new Long Range Platform launches across Nigeria. You will own country-level readiness for multiple concurrent site launches—making launch decisions, driving cross-functional alignment, and raising the operational bar so sites launch faster, safer, and scale reliably. This work directly enables Zipline’s mission to build an instant delivery system that delivers critical medical and commercial goods across hard-to-reach regions; your success reduces time-to-service, increases launch reliability, and ensures safe, certified flight operations in challenging field environments.
What You'll Do
Own end-to-end operational readiness for 3–6 concurrent Long Range Platform site launches across Nigeria, from planning through first flight and early stabilization; maintain an integrated program plan with milestones, dependencies, risks, and mitigation actions.
Define and enforce clear go/no-go criteria and measurable acceptance standards for safety, staffing, training & certification, infrastructure, equipment, communications, power, charging systems, and first-flight procedures.
Maintain and report against launch KPIs (e.g., staffing readiness %, certification completion %, equipment acceptance pass rate, launch go/no-go rate) and use those metrics to stop or green-light launches.
Lead the cross-functional readiness cadence and day-to-day decision rhythm, driving alignment between Recruiting, Academy, Engineering, Construction, Supply Chain, Safety/Regulatory, Partnerships, and Country Leadership; resolve conflicts and escalate issues with clear decision requests.
Validate readiness through field verification: lead on-site checkouts, acceptance tests, and flight-readiness demonstrations; identify and close launch-critical gaps before first flight.

About Glome Health
Glome Health is a health technology startup improving access to kidney care across Africa. We develop and commercialize peritoneal dialysis products, working with manufacturers, regulators, and healthcare providers across multiple regions. We are a small, fast-moving, largely remote team — and this role is our hands-on support on the ground in Lagos.
The Role
The Operations Coordinator keeps day-to-day operations running. You will own a set of recurring processes — trackers, meeting coordination, records, deadlines, and follow-ups — and run them dependably with regular guidance from the leadership team. You resolve routine exceptions yourself and escalate material issues early.
This is a strong fit for a structured, resourceful early-career operator who enjoys bringing order to busy workstreams, communicates clearly, and follows tasks through to completion. You do not need a biomedical/health sciences background for this role — we work with specialists/consultants across domains like regulatory, legal, and payroll — but you must be willing to learn the language and operating requirements of a regulated healthcare business.
What You'll Do
Trackers and follow-through: maintain project trackers, action logs, and decision records; chase owners for updates — who owes what by when — and flag risks and slippage to leadership early.
Meetings and coordination: schedule meetings across the team, consultants, vendors, and time zones; prepare agendas, take clear notes, circulate action items, and follow them up to closure.
Deadlines and obligations: run the calendar of recurring obligations — corporate filings, renewals, statutory submissions, and payments — so nothing is missed.
Documents and records: keep corporate, regulatory, and operational records organized and findable; prepare and route document packages for signing, notarization, and submission; support NAFDAC, ethics, quality, or partner reviews by collecting and filing what the specialist leads need.
Manufacturing and clinical support: under direction, track production schedules, shipments, and supplier documentation, and support clinical-program logistics — training coordination, study materials, and document collection.
Company operations: coordinate schedules, travel, procurement, invoices, and reimbursements; support onboarding, HR records, and payroll coordination.
Expense and reporting support: keep clean expense records, reconcile invoices and payment status, and help prepare concise internal status updates.
Routine problem-solving: resolve routine exceptions yourself, suggest simple improvements to templates and checklists, and escalate anything material.
What Success Looks Like
In the first 30 days, you know the company's priorities, partners, and core documents, and the action tracker and deadline calendar are reliably current.
Within 90 days, leadership trusts the trackers: meetings produce circulated action items, recurring obligations happen on time, and follow-ups close without repeated prompting.
Within 6–12 months, you run your recurring processes dependably with minimal guidance and are taking on larger workstreams — building toward Associate-level scope.
What We're Looking For
Roughly 1–3 years of experience in operations, administration, project coordination, or programme roles — exceptional fresh graduates considered.
No particular degree is required — we care about track record and judgment. Backgrounds in business, operations, health sciences, public health, or supply chain all work.
Demonstrated follow-through: accurate records, closed loops, and tasks completed without repeated prompting.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including clear meeting notes, professional emails, trackers, and short reports.
High proficiency with spreadsheets, shared documents, presentations, and common collaboration tools — including AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) in day-to-day work.
Sound judgment, discretion, and comfort handling commercially sensitive or confidential information.
Ability to work effectively with senior professionals, consultants, vendors, and external partners across organizations and time zones.
Based in Lagos or able to work regularly in Lagos, with willingness to travel within Nigeria as the project requires.
Helpful, but Not Required
Experience in medical devices, pharmaceuticals, clinical research, dialysis, healthcare delivery, or regulated manufacturing.
Familiarity with NAFDAC, Nigerian ethics-review processes, Good Clinical Practice, quality systems, procurement, logistics, or inventory management.
Experience working with hospitals, research institutions, manufacturers, distributors, funders, or international partners.
Formal training or certification in project management, operations, supply chain, clinical research, or quality management.
How We Work
Own the outcome:
we take responsibility for getting important work across the finish line.
Be rigorous:
in healthcare, details, documentation, and follow-through matter.
Communicate early:
we surface risks and uncertainty before they become delays or surprises.
Stay resourceful:
we solve problems thoughtfully, even when time, resources, or information are limited.
Keep patients in view:
operational decisions ultimately affect whether safer kidney care reaches the people who need it.
What We Offer
A hands-on role in building a mission-driven health technology company at a pivotal stage of growth.
Direct exposure to healthcare product development, manufacturing, clinical programs, commercialization, and cross-border partnerships.
Meaningful responsibility, close collaboration with company leadership, and a defined growth ladder — Coordinator to Associate to Specialist — as the company scales.

**Role Description**


The Engine Room Superintendent heads the FSO engine room operations; he is directly responsible for the operation of all main and auxiliary machinery systems, including engine control room (ECR) operations. He will supervise all aspects of maintenance requirements in the Engine Room in conjunction with FSO Maintenance Supervisor. Specific areas of responsibilities will include:

* Prompt and efficient reporting of all defects that may affect the safety or operational efficiency of the FSO


* Oversee operation and maintenance of all mechanical equipment, including engines, boilers, compressors, turbines, pumps, separators, HVAC systems and others


* Supervise maintenance in line with OEM manuals, class rules, and safety standards.


* Execute preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance strategies to ensure equipment continuous availability.


* Monitor critical systems including power generation, inert gas, cargo offloading, SW Cooling, firewater systems, etc.


* Lead and enforce PTW systems, safety talks, JSA reviews, and hazard assessments.


* Interpret P\&IDs, OEM documents, and technical drawings for troubleshooting and repairs.


* Direct daily activities of Engine Room staff, technicians and third\-party contractors in normal operations and during shutdowns or critical maintenance.


* Support the Material Coordinator in spare parts inventory and procurement processes.


* Participate in Root Cause Failure Analyses and incident investigations.


* Coordinate with Maintenance and Deck Operations Teams on integrated operations.


* Support commissioning, start\-up, and testing of overhauled or new equipment and mechanical systems.


* Maintain logs, equipment history records, and daily operational reports.


* Ensure emergency systems (e.g., fire pumps, Emergency Generator) are always ready for deployment.


* Mentor junior engineers and ER staff to support skill development.

* Class I (Unlimited) Chief Engineer Certificate of Competency (CoC) in accordance with STCW requirements.
* Minimum of **10 years' experience as Chief Engineer** on steam\-driven VLCCs, FSOs, FPSOs, or similar offshore marine vessels.
* Proven experience managing engine room operations, power generation systems, boilers, turbines, pumps, compressors, HVAC, and auxiliary machinery.
* Strong knowledge of planned maintenance systems (PMS), preventive and corrective maintenance, and equipment reliability management.
* Good understanding of SOLAS, MARPOL, ISM Code, Class Society requirements, and Flag State regulations.
* Demonstrated leadership experience supervising engine room personnel and managing contractors in offshore or marine environments.
* Experience with Permit to Work (PTW), Job Safety Analysis (JSA), Risk Assessment, Lock\-Out/Tag\-Out (LOTO), and other HSE management systems.
* Ability to read and interpret P\&IDs, engineering drawings, OEM manuals, and technical documentation.
* Experience supporting commissioning, equipment start\-up, troubleshooting, and Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA).
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS).
* Excellent communication, leadership, planning, and problem\-solving skills.
* Valid STCW certification and a valid seafarer's medical certificate.
* Offshore certifications such as **BOSIET/FOET with CA\-EBS** and a valid offshore medical certificate will be an added advantage.
* Must be eligible to work in Nigeria.

Job Title: Senior Supply Chain Specialist
Location:
Apapa, Lagos

Job Overview
The Senior Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for coordinating end-to-end import logistics, regulatory compliance, and supply chain operations to ensure the timely and cost-effective movement of cargo from origin to final delivery.
The role oversees shipping documentation, customs and regulatory approvals, stakeholder coordination, and compliance with all statutory requirements while driving operational excellence and customer satisfaction.
The role will also serve as the Company's subject matter expert on regulatory compliance, managing all documentation and approvals required by NAFDAC, SON, NESREA, NAQS, Nigeria Customs Service, and other government agencies to facilitate seamless cargo clearance.
Key Responsibilities
Supply Chain & Shipment Coordination:
Coordinate the movement of import shipments from origin to final destination.
Monitor shipment milestones and proactively resolve operational bottlenecks.
Coordinate with shipping lines, freight forwarders, transporters, terminals, and customs agents to ensure timely cargo movement.
Ensure accurate documentation throughout the supply chain process.
Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency.

NESREA permits where applicable.
NAQS import permits and quarantine documentation.
Review shipping documents to ensure regulatory compliance before submission.

Process Consignment References for regulated cargo.
Monitor approval status and resolve system validation issues promptly.
Liaise with regulatory agencies to expedite endorsements and Full Releases.

Federal Ministry of Environment and other relevant agencies.

Verify HS Codes and determine applicable regulatory requirements.
Ensure all regulatory approvals are obtained before cargo arrival whenever possible.
Identify compliance risks and recommend corrective actions.

Provide regulatory guidance to Operations, Business Development, and Key Account teams.
Support Form M, PAAR, and customs documentation processes.
Resolve regulatory-related shipment delays.
Escalate complex operational or compliance issues to Management promptly.
Client & Stakeholder Management:

Communicate documentation requirements clearly and promptly.
Provide regular shipment and approval status updates.

Job Description
Job Opportunity: Technical Project Manager (EPC / Oil & Gas)
Company: Riglog Services Limited
Location: Udu, Delta State Nigeria
Job Type: Full-Time
Industry: Oil & Gas (Upstream / Midstream EPC, Pipeline Construction & Fabrication)
About Us
Riglog Services Limited is a premier engineering and oilfield services company. We deliver high-quality Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC), pipeline installation, structural fabrication, and facility maintenance solutions. We are seeking a highly competent, technically sound Technical Project Manager to drive our project execution from inception to delivery.
The Role
As the Technical Project Manager, you will be the core execution engine of our projects. You will oversee operations from start to finish, beginning with the competitive tendering stage, through detailed engineering design planning, to on-site field execution. You will work closely with our Senior Project Engineer and act as the primary technical interface for our clients and regulatory bodies.
Key Responsibilities
End-to-End Tendering: Review client RFQs/ITTs and lead the development of technical and commercial bid proposals.
Project Planning & Execution: Create detailed project schedules, budgets, procurement plans, and resource allocation strategies from start to finish.
Technical Oversight: Provide deep technical direction on pipeline construction, asset integrity, and fabrication works, ensuring alignment with engineering designs.
Client & Stakeholder Relations: Lead progress meetings, defend technical variations, and represent the company professionally to IOCs, NOCs, and subcontractors.
Field & Team Coordination: Supervise project teams and coordinate closely with the Senior Project Engineer to ensure safe, on-time, and within-budget delivery.
QA/QC & HSE Compliance: Enforce strict adherence to ISO standards, safety protocols, and local content regulations.
Requirements & Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical, Civil, Electrical, or Petroleum Engineering. (PMP or COREN registration is a strong plus).
Experience: 5+ years of verifiable experience managing EPC or pipeline construction projects in the Nigerian oil and gas sector.
Technical Soundness: Exceptional ability to interpret engineering drawings (P&IDs, Isometrics), technical specifications, and project scopes.
Bidding Expertise: Proven track record of successfully bidding and winning contracts via NipeX or direct tender boards.
Soft Skills: Outstanding communication, sharp negotiation skills, and a strong presence in high-level stakeholder meetings.
How To Apply
Interested and qualified candidates should send their updated CV and a cover letter detailing their tendering and project delivery experience to ,and cc: with the subject line "Technical Project Manager”.
Application Deadline: 3 August, 2026
Pay: ₦450,000.00 - ₦650,000.00 per month
Work Location: In person

About the Role
The Regional Commercial Manager - Phones, WCA is a commercial leadership role responsible for driving device sales growth, revenue performance, and market expansion across West and Central Africa. This role sits at the intersection of sales, partnerships, product, supply chain, and marketing – serving as the primary commercial owner for PayGo smartphone business in the region.The ideal candidate is a commercially driven, analytically sharp, and highly collaborative leader with deep experience in the mobile devices ecosystem across sub-Saharan Africa.
Key Responsibilities:
● Own regional commercial targets — jointly with the sales team
This role shares revenue and unit sales targets with the field sales team across West and Central Africa. The sales team, which reports into its own sales leadership hierarchy, owns day-to-day execution on the ground. The commercial manager's job is to create the conditions for that team to succeed — ensuring they have the right products, the right pricing, the right channel coverage, and the right marketing support to hit shared goals.
● Track performance and drive course correction
Monitor revenue performance across markets in close coordination with the sales team. Where performance is off-track, this role diagnoses the root cause — whether commercial, operational, or market-driven — and works with the relevant teams to respond.
● Build and manage OEM and distributor partnerships
Partners with phone brands (OEMs) and local distributors to stock and sell devices. This role manages those partnerships, negotiates terms, and
ensures the right phones are available in the right places at the right time.
● Develop and commercialise telecom partnerships across the region
Mobile network operators have distribution networks, marketing channels, and customer relationships that took years to build. This role is responsible for identifying the right MNO partners in each market, understanding the full breadth of what a partnership could unlock, and structuring deals that translate that potential into tangible commercial outcomes — with the nature of each partnership varying by market and operator.
● Manage product availability and lifecycle transitions
Getting the right phones into the right markets at the right time is a critical commercial lever. This role works closely with supply chain to maintain forecast accuracy, ensure stock availability, and plan new model launches — while managing the phase-out of older models carefully enough to avoid dead stock
● Drive regional marketing and go-to-market execution
Translating a commercial plan into market-level impact requires more than a good product and a willing sales team. This role works closely with marketing to ensure promotional campaigns, digital advertising, in-store merchandising, and go-to-market plans are localised, well-executed, and pulling in the same direction — converting awareness into sales across every touchpoint in the region.
● Champion an effective after-sales experience for customers
In a PAYGo model, the relationship with the customer doesn't end at the point of sale — it spans the entire repayment period. This role works closely with the after-sales team to ensure policies, processes, and service standards are fair to the customer and commercially sound, advocating for improvements where gaps exist and holding partners accountable to agreed service levels.
Requirements
Experience:
● 10+ years in a commercial, sales, or business development role within consumer electronics, mobile devices, telecoms, or a similarly fast-moving consumer industry
● Proven track record of delivering against revenue and unit sales targets in a structure where execution is shared with a separate sales team
● Experience managing OEM, distributor, and/or telecom partnerships — including negotiating commercial terms and managing performance over time
● Demonstrated ability to operate across multiple markets in West and Central Africa, navigating different regulatory environments, trade dynamics, and consumer behaviours
● Experience working cross-functionally — particularly bridging sales, marketing, supply chain, and product teams around a shared commercial plan
● Familiarity with device financing, PAYGo, or other consumer credit models is a strong advantage
● Proficiency in French is highly advantageous given the markets in scope
Skills:
● Analytical thinking: identifying what is driving or undermining performance, and acting on it
● Go-to-market execution: understands how to localise a commercial plan — pricing, promotions, merchandising, and channel activation — for diverse markets
● Partner management: able to build and sustain productive relationships with OEMs, distributors, and MNOs — and structure deals that deliver on paper and in the market
● Cross-functional coordination: effective at aligning teams that don't report into this role, and resolving upstream blockers that the sales team cannot solve themselves
● Communication: able to present commercial performance and market insight clearly to senior stakeholders, and translate strategic direction into plans that field teams can execute

The Importation Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and controlling all import activities to ensure the timely, compliant, and cost-effective supply of imported products to the company's warehouse. The role ensures full compliance with Nigerian customs regulations while optimizing lead times, inventory availability, and import costs.
