The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
The International Rescue Committee has been in Nigeria since October 2012, in response to flooding that impacted several states of Nigeria, by responding in Kogi state. The IRC has since expanded its humanitarian operations across Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) states, as well as Zamfara, Sokoto and Katsina states, responding to the needs of displaced and vulnerable communities in the Northeast and Northwest. The IRC has been working in partnership with multiple international donors, government agencies and local partners to implement multi-sectoral and integrated programming covering nutrition, environmental health/WASH, health, education, women empowerment, economic recovery, protection, and other related services. IRC Nigeria now operates a country office in Abuja with field offices in Mubi and Yola of Adamawa State, Maiduguri, Monguno, and Gwoza of Borno State in Northeast Nigeria, Gusau, Sokoto, and Katsina in Northwestern Nigeria.
Scope Of Work
The Governance team of the International Rescue Committee, via power integration, amplifies the voices of people whose lives have been impacted by conflict and crisis. We help them regain control of their future by championing their rights to influence the decisions that affect their cities, towns, and communities.
To achieve this, we
strengthen
the ability and power of people affected by conflict and crisis to have a voice in how decisions are made in their communities. We also
support
governments, civil society organizations, community representatives, and the IRC to respond to their voices and provide effective and inclusive services and
promote
communication between leaders and the people they represent, so that actions are meaningful and sustainable.
In line with the current IRC’s Strategic Action Plan (SAP) agenda, which is to have governance programming integrated across sectors, the Governance Manager will support integrating power across all program outcome areas.
Job Overview / Summary
The Governance Manager will provide strategic leadership and oversight for the implementation of governance programming across multiple grants within the IRC Nigeria Country Program. The role is responsible for ensuring the effective integration of governance and power approaches across sectors, including Health, Nutrition, WASH, ERD, and Protection.
The Governance Manager will lead day-to-day supervision of governance teams, manage program delivery, oversee grant implementation and compliance, and ensure strong stakeholder engagement at all levels. The position requires a dynamic and experienced professional capable of promoting accountability, strengthening systems, and fostering inclusive governance practices while ensuring high-quality program implementation, budget management, and reporting.
Responsibilities
Program Management & Development:
Develop and implement detailed work plans, spending plans, and procurement plans, along with supporting systems, to ensure timely delivery of project outputs and achievement of targets.
Contribute to the design and development of proposals, budgets, and concept notes in close coordination with the Governance lead.
Support the effective implementation of the Power Integration Strategy for the Nigeria Country Program, ensuring alignment across governance and sectoral interventions.
Collaborate closely with the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) team to track performance, ensuring that power-related indicators and targets are achieved and documented.
Produce timely, high-quality, and results-based reports, including annual work plans, monitoring and tracking matrices, implementation plans, and other required project narratives and updates.
Establish and maintain strong working relationships with key stakeholders, including government institutions, legislators, international and local NGOs, as well as women’s and youth organizations, to support policy influence and program impact.
Conduct regular field monitoring visits across all intervention locations to ensure program quality, compliance with standards, and alignment with donor requirements.
Grants Management And Reporting
Assist with the overall management and oversight of grants, including the development and maintenance of detailed work plans, spending plans, and procurement plans for all projects.
Actively participate in Grant Opening, Mid-Term Review, and Closing meetings, ensuring alignment with donor requirements and IRC standards.
Prepare and submit high-quality internal and external reports within agreed timelines, using IRC and donor-approved formats and guidelines.
Ensure the effective implementation and use of Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) systems throughout the lifecycle of governance projects, promoting data-driven decision-making and accountability.
Oversee project budget management by regularly reviewing Budget vs. Actual reports, weekly consolidated reports, and expenditure tracking sheets.
Work in close collaboration with the Finance and Supply Chain teams to ensure accurate financial reporting, timely procurement, and compliance with organizational and donor policies.
Identify and proactively address risks related to budget utilization, grant compliance, and reporting to ensure smooth project implementation.
Staff Management, Learning & Development
Support the recruitment of national staff in coordination with the Human Resources Department, ensuring transparent and merit-based processes.
Maintain up-to-date job descriptions, participate in interviews, and ensure comprehensive onboarding and orientation of new staff to IRC systems, values, and the Governance program.
Provide strong leadership, supervision, and technical guidance to Governance team members through regular check-ins, performance feedback, and supportive mentoring.
Set clear performance objectives, conduct regular performance reviews, and support staff through coaching, mentoring, and capacity-building initiatives.
Identify capacity gaps and design targeted learning and development initiatives to strengthen staff competencies and program delivery.
Deliver and facilitate capacity-strengthening activities for staff and community structures on advocacy, stakeholder engagement, accountability mechanisms, and community liaison approaches.
Provide ongoing technical support to field teams to enhance effective community engagement, representation, and inclusive participation strategies.
Promote a culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and adherence to IRC’s principles, safeguarding standards, and professional ethics.
Representation & Coordination
Establish and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with government entities, community leaders, civil society organizations, donors, UN agencies, and other key stakeholders.
Represent IRC in coordination platforms, technical working groups, community meetings, and stakeholder forums, as delegated.
Support the design and implementation of advocacy initiatives, including events, campaigns, policy dialogues, and community engagement activities.
Strengthen IRC’s visibility and reputation through effective, professional representation and proactive stakeholder engagement.
Facilitate clear, consistent communication and collaboration between IRC and community structures to enhance program acceptance, participation, and access.
Provide capacity building and technical support on governance and power integration for designated focal persons, while monitoring their activities and tracking progress.
Promote knowledge sharing and system strengthening by supporting local partners, government institutions, and community groups to build sustainable governance structures.
Collaborate closely with IRC’s emergency response teams to integrate governance and power approaches into emergency programming through context analysis, stakeholder mapping, and relevant assessments.
Key Working Relationships
Position Reports to:
Governance Coordinator and Field Coordinator Maiduguri
Position directly supervises:
Governance Officers
Other Internal And/or External Contacts
Internal:
Supply Chain and Finance, Regional Policy Advisors, HQ Technical Advisors
External:
Service providers, Traditional and Community Leaders, Local Government Authorities, Government Ministries/Agencies
Qualification/Experience
Bachelor’s Degree in Community Development, Public Administration, Law, Project Management, or other relevant field; or Minimum three (3) years of experience in governance programming, social accountability, public administration, institutional development, public-sector capacity building or related technical areas.
Strong knowledge and understanding of governance and power integration in service delivery, particularly Health, Nutrition, WASH, ERD, and Protection
Experience with Systems Strengthening approaches such as Organizational Development (OD), Problem-Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA), Community Scorecards, and durable solutions.
Proven ability to work effectively with government institutions, civil society organizations, and community stakeholders, demonstrated ability to negotiate and partner with communities, civil society, and government representatives.
Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Fluency in written and spoken Hausa and Kanuri is preferred.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 50% of the time, including field locations.
PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Job Summary
The S&OP Manager leads the end‑to‑end Sales & Operations Planning process to deliver a single, aligned plan across Demand, Supply, Finance, and Commercial. The role is accountable for balancing customer service, cost, and inventory, and for providing the leadership team with a clear, data‑driven view of risks, opportunities, and trade‑offs.
Key Responsibilities
1. S&OP Strategy and Governance
Design, implement, and continuously improve a robust monthly S&OP cycle (demand review, supply review, pre‑S&OP, executive S&OP).
Establish and maintain S&OP governance: calendar, agendas, data standards, decision rights, and escalation paths.
Ensure the S&OP process is fully aligned with business strategy, budget, and long‑range plan (capacity, capex, and portfolio).
2. Demand Planning and Consensus
Lead the demand planning process with Sales, Marketing, and Finance to generate a realistic, unconstrained demand plan.
Challenge and validate forecasts using historical data, market intelligence, promotions, and seasonality.
Facilitate consensus forecasting, ensuring one agreed demand plan is signed off and used across the business.
Track forecast accuracy and bias, and drive root‑cause analysis and corrective actions.
3. Supply Planning and Capacity Management
Coordinate with Manufacturing, Procurement, and Logistics to create an optimized supply plan that meets demand within capacity and cost constraints.
Ensure rough‑cut capacity planning (RCCP) is in place and aligned with labour, line, and supplier capabilities.
Identify and quantify supply constraints, risks, and bottlenecks, and propose mitigation scenarios (e.g., overtime, subcontracting, alternative sourcing, inventory strategies).
Align medium‑ to long‑term capacity needs with capex and resource planning.
4. Integrated Business Planning & Financial Alignment
Ensure the S&OP process is tightly integrated with financial planning (revenue, margin, and working‑capital targets).
Provide a rolling 3–18‑month view of volume/value, highlighting gaps to budget and scenario options.
Work closely with Finance to translate volume plans into financial projections and support decision‑making on trade‑offs (service vs. cost vs. cash).
5. Inventory and Service Optimization
Define and maintain inventory policies (safety stock, reorder points, minimum order quantities, coverage days) for raw materials, WIP, and FG.
Balance customer service levels (OTIF) against inventory and operating costs, using data‑driven segmentation (ABC/XYZ, make‑to‑stock vs. make‑to‑order, etc.).
Monitor and improve key metrics: OTIF, stockouts, excess and obsolete stock (E&O), days of inventory (DOI), and expedited freight.
6. Data, Systems, and Analytics
Own the data and assumptions feeding the S&OP process (historical sales, pipeline, capacities, lead times, yields, BOMs).
Drive effective use and continuous improvement of planning tools (ERP/MRP, APS, demand planning software, BI dashboards).
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports that provide clear visibility on demand, supply, inventory, and S&OP performance.
Champion data quality and master data governance in collaboration with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance.
7. Stakeholder Management and Change Leadership
Act as the central orchestrator between Commercial, Operations, Procurement, Finance, and Logistics to ensure alignment and ownership of the plan.
Facilitate S&OP meetings at all levels, ensuring they are decision‑focused, time‑efficient, and supported by clear analyses.
Drive a culture of accountability and transparency, where assumptions, risks, and decisions are clearly documented.
Lead change management for S&OP‑related initiatives, ensuring adoption of new processes, tools, and behaviors.
Qualifications and Experience
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, Economics, or related field.
Postgraduate degree (MBA/MSc) is an advantage; Professional Certifications (preferred)
Experience:
6+ years in Supply Chain, Planning, or Operations, with at least 3–5 years directly leading S&OP or integrated planning.
Experience in manufacturing/FMCG/CPG or similar high‑volume, SKU‑rich environment.
Proven track record improving forecast accuracy, service levels, and inventory performance.
Technical Skills:
Strong knowledge of demand and supply planning concepts (MRP, DRP, RCCP, safety‑stock methods, ABC/XYZ, etc.).
Hands‑on experience with ERP systems (e.g., Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics) and planning tools (APS, demand planning software).
Advanced Excel and analytics skills; experience with BI tools (Power BI) is a strong plus.
Comfortable building and explaining scenarios, sensitivities, and trade‑off analyses.
Soft Skills:
Excellent facilitation and stakeholder management skills; able to challenge and influence senior leaders respectfully.
Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and structured thinking abilities.
Clear communication and storytelling, able to convert complex data into simple, actionable insights.
High ownership, resilience, and bias for action in a fast‑changing environment.
<

description:

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented FP&A Analyst to join our Finance team.
The FP&A Analyst is responsible for leading financial planning and analysis activities for d.light Nigeria, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives and supporting business growth. Cash Management
Manage daily cash transactions, ensuring proper recording and reconciliation.
Perform regular bank reconciliations to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Monitor and forecast cash flow to maintain sufficient liquidity for operations.
Ensure adherence to cash handling policies and internal financial controls.
Inventory Management

Conduct regular inventory audits to identify discrepancies and implement corrective actions.
Support procurement by ensuring timely payments and monitoring stock replenishment.
Work with the finance and supply chain teams to align inventory valuation with financial reporting.
Reconciliation and Reporting
Prepare and reconcile cash, bank accounts, and inventory records.
Assist the Senior Accountant in generating reports related to cash flow and inventory status.
Identify and escalate risks related to cash handling and inventory management.
Internal Controls and Compliance
Implement and monitor internal controls related to cash and inventory processes.
Ensure compliance with company financial policies, local tax laws, and statutory regulations.
Support audit processes by providing necessary documentation and reconciliations.
Requirements
Desired Skills and Experience
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Supply Chain Management, or a related field.
Experience
Minimum of 2 years of experience in cash management, inventory control, or a similar role.
Experience working with cash management and inventory tracking software.
Familiarity with ERP systems and financial reporting tools are an advantage.
Knowledge of Kenyan tax regulations is a plus.
Skills and Competencies
Technical Skills
Strong reconciliation skills with high attention to detail.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial/inventory management systems.
Ability to analyze financial and inventory data to identify trends and discrepancies.

Role Purpose
Save the Children Nigeria is implementing a two-year ECHO-HIP-funded integrated Education in Emergencies (EiE) and Child Protection response project in Yobe and Katsina States, aimed at restoring safe, inclusive, and protective learning environments for crisis-affected girls and boys, including children with disabilities.
The programme combines Accelerated Basic Education for out-of-school and overage learners with Literacy/Numeracy Boost and Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approaches in formal schools to support learning recovery, reduce dropout, and promote reintegration into education. School safety and safeguarding will be strengthened through teacher training, child help desks, and risk-informed programming. In addition, the rehabilitation of classrooms and WASH in Schools infrastructure will improve safety, accessibility, ventilation, and lighting, including disability-friendly features such as ramps to the leaners.
The WASH and Construction Officer will be responsible for the technical oversight of all construction-related activities, including feasibility assessments, design preparation, BoQ development, tender documentation, and procurement support in collaboration with the Supply Chain team. The role will also provide supervision of contractors, conduct regular field monitoring, and ensure compliance with SCI construction standards in close coordination with the Education team, Supply Chain and relevant stakeholders in Katsina and Yobe States.

Day 60: Augmentin pilot landed and selling through 50 pilot pharmacies; Ceftriaxone pilot batch (5,000) ordered.
Day 90: Ceftriaxone pilot delivered; sell-through and reorder measured; landed cost confirmed against quotes; Go/No-Go pack for the CEO.
Who You Are
8–15 years in pharmaceutical manufacturing or supply chain in Nigeria / West Africa.
Direct NAFDAC product-registration experience (you have filed and landed registrations).
Existing relationships with contract manufacturers — local and international (India, China, Egypt, Pakistan).
Step-up candidate preferred: currently a Plant Manager or Supply Chain Director who sees this as a Head/VP move.
Numerate — comfortable owning a landed-cost model and defending margin to the CEO.

Company Description
RxAll™ is a digital healthcare infrastructure platform focused on enabling on-demand access to high-quality medicines at manufacturer or wholesale prices for hospitals, pharmacies, and patients. Through a curated network of reputable wholesalers and pharmaceutical companies, RxAll addresses the global challenge of access to affordable, safe drugs. Its technology stack includes RxScanner™, an instant drug testing platform for authenticating medicines, RxPOS™ for in-store and online inventory and sales management, and RxDelivered™ as a marketplace for seamless distribution. RxPay™ provides embedded fintech solutions to finance invoices, improving availability and affordability of medicines for B2B2C customers. The company’s vision is to achieve universal access to high-quality medicines at the lowest possible prices worldwide, starting with Africa.
Role Summary
RxAll is moving upstream from pharmacy credit and distribution into own-brand contract manufacturing and parallel import of pharmaceutical products for Nigeria and West Africa. The Head of Manufacturing / Supply Chain owns this build end-to-end so the CEO can stay on the core business. This is the first and most important hire in the initiative.
Reports to Founder/CEO
Location Ibadan (with supplier travel)

Sourcing: shortlist and manage contract manufacturers (offshore + in-country); negotiate EXW/landed pricing to hit ≥30% gross margin.
Regulatory: drive NAFDAC registration for own-brand products; coordinate GMP audits, COPP, dossiers (with a consultant).
Landed-cost model: own and validate the unit economics — manufacturing, freight, duties, NAFDAC amortization, distribution.
Pilots: run the Ceftriaxone and Augmentin/Ozempic pilots through RxAllDelivered; track sell-through, reorder, and margin.
Supply chain: inventory planning, QA on arrival (batch testing), 3PL and warehousing, supplier portal for invoices/COAs/shipping docs.

Day 30: validated landed-cost model; EXW locked for ≥30% gross margin on Ceftriaxone; NAFDAC filing opened; Augmentin parallel-import pilot order (1,000 packs) placed.
Day 60: Augmentin pilot landed and selling through 50 pilot pharmacies; Ceftriaxone pilot batch (5,000) ordered.

8–15 years in pharmaceutical manufacturing or supply chain in Nigeria / West Africa.
Direct NAFDAC product-registration experience (you have filed and landed registrations).
Existing relationships with contract manufacturers — local and international (India, China, Egypt, Pakistan).
Step-up candidate preferred: currently a Plant Manager or Supply Chain Director who sees this as a Head/VP move.
Numerate — comfortable owning a landed-cost model and defending margin to the CEO.
**Hiring Rules **
Step-up candidates preferred (one level below, 5–8 years, sees this as a promotion).

About ProtocolClear
ProtocolClear is an independent, principal-led consultancy in security, privacy, AI governance, and compliance. We deliver security and compliance engagements to clients in regulated industries and run an in-house team in Lagos. This role exists so AI-security delivery can be handed to a capable senior practitioner, with the founder, a former principal security architect for AI/ML security, overseeing quality. Security made clear is the standard every deliverable must meet.
About the role
This is a salaried AI-security delivery consultant role, distinct from our annotation roles. You will run and contribute to client engagements focused on the security of AI and machine learning systems: securing LLMs, generative and agentic AI applications, threat modeling AI platforms, reviewing model and data pipelines, and building AI governance programs aligned with recognized frameworks. You will work alongside the privacy and security consultants and take on internal work when not on client delivery. You will be client-facing: scoping engagements, explaining findings, prioritizing remediation, and guiding clients to defensible outcomes. The founder oversees delivery and supplies direction, and over time, you carry more of the engagement load directly.
The standard your work is held to
Your work is held to a professional consulting standard: findings must be accurate, evidence-based, and defensible to a client's auditor, board, or regulator. An AI-security recommendation must be correct and implementable, not generic. A control gap must map to a specific framework requirement and to a real, prioritized remediation. You are expected to tell a client what is actually wrong in their AI system and what to do about it, in plain terms, without overstating risk to sell work or understating it to avoid a hard conversation. You own the quality of what leaves your hands. Certifications are verified before hire, and your delivery is expected to match your credentials.
What you will do
Secure LLM and generative AI applications: prompt injection and indirect prompt injection defense, output handling, sensitive-information-disclosure controls, and guardrail design.
Assess agentic AI and tool-use systems against the OWASP Agentic Top 10, covering goal hijack, tool misuse, excessive agency, memory and context poisoning, and insecure inter-agent communication.
Review RAG pipeline security: retrieval and embedding poisoning, vector-store access control, cross-tenant isolation, and data leakage through context.
Threat model AI platforms and test adversarial ML risks: data and model poisoning, model extraction and inversion, membership inference, and evasion.
Review MLOps and AI supply-chain security, including model provenance, ML-BOM, pipeline and CI/CD security, and third-party model vetting.
Assess multi-tenant inference isolation and cloud security architecture for AI workloads across AWS, Azure, GCP, or OCI.
Run AI red-teaming and model evaluation using the OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Agentic Top 10, and MITRE ATLAS.
Design AI governance programs aligned to NIST AI RMF, NIST AI 600-1, ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act, and align them to Nigeria's NDPA, NDPC, and CBN requirements, including DPIAs and algorithmic auditing.
Run AI risk assessments and translate them into prioritized, business-aware remediation plans.
Write clear findings, present them to technical and non-technical stakeholders, and carry out internal security work when not on a billable client delivery.
What we are looking for (required)
Three to seven years of experience in cybersecurity, cloud security, or application security, with demonstrable hands-on AI/ML security work, not just study.
A working command of AI-security concepts: LLM and agent risks, prompt injection, RAG and data-pipeline security, and AI governance frameworks.
Fluency in the OWASP LLM Top 10 and NIST AI RMF.
Practical cloud security knowledge across at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, GCP, or OCI).
Python.
The ability to run a threat model or risk assessment and produce a prioritized remediation plan without supervision.
Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining an AI-security control to a non-technical client and writing regulator-grade reports.
A professional-level security certification, verified before hire.
Willingness to have certifications and references verified as part of hiring.
Nice to have (preferred)
IAPP AIGP (AI Governance Professional) or ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Implementer.
Senior security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CCSP.
Cloud security certifications such as AWS Security Specialty, Azure AZ-500, or SC-200.
Hands-on experience with LLM or agentic systems, RAG pipelines, or MLOps security.

**HIRING – Head, Structured Trade and Commodity Finance (Financial Services)**  



Location: Lagos  

  



Department: Investment Banking  

  



Reporting Line: CEO  

  



**Compensation:** N120,000,000\.00 – N150,000,000\.00 Annually \+ other benefits  

  



**About the Company:** Our client is a leading financial bank with a strong presence across Nigeria. The company is committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences, driving financial inclusion, and maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and regulatory compliance.  

  



Our client is seeking to hire a dynamic and visionary executive to Head our Structured Trade and Commodity Finance (“STCF”) business who will be responsible for driving the growth, strategy, and performance of our STCF business. This position demands a blend of strategic acumen, deep technical expertise, broad relationship network (with financiers and participants across the commodity value\-chain) and exceptional leadership to propel our STCF business forward in a competitive global environment.  

  



The role provides strategic leadership in originating new business, managing risk, coordinating cross\-functional teams, and positioning the bank as the preferred financial partner for high\-growth businesses.  

  



The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the hiring and growth of a high\-performing team, foster innovation in complex financial instruments, and ensure alignment with regulatory standards and market opportunities in Nigeria and the broader African context.  

  



**Key Responsibilities**  



* **Strategic Leadership and Business Development:** Develop and execute the overall strategy for the STCF Division, identifying new market opportunities, product innovations, and revenue streams tailored to Nigerian and African markets. Originate structured transactions with mid\-tier to large corporate producers, multinational traders (soft and hard commodities), Oil \& Gas downstream players and state\-owned entities just to name a few.
* **Team Management and Talent Development:** Lead a multidisciplinary team of professionals including structurers, analysts, and legal/compliance experts. Foster a collaborative culture, mentor high\-potential talent, and ensure succession planning to build a resilient organization, with an emphasis on local talent development.
* **Product Innovation and Execution:** Oversee the origination and structuring of commodity finance solutions including pre\-export finance (PXF), borrowing base facilities, prepayment structures, and warehouse receipt financing, as well as other bespoke structured solutions adapted to regional needs. Ensure seamless execution from origination to distribution, collaborating with the Sales \& Trading team, and Syndication Teams including leading capital\-raising efforts by syndicating deals with local commercial banks, international lenders, and Development Finance Institutions.
* **Risk Management and Compliance:** In conjunction with the Risk \& Compliance team, design and implement robust risk frameworks for STCF transactions, including credit, market, operational, and liquidity risks. Ensure full compliance with Nigerian regulations (e.g., SEC Nigeria, CBN guidelines) as well as global standards (e.g., Basel III, Dodd\-Frank, MiFID II) and internal policies, while mitigating potential legal and reputational risks.
* **Client Engagement and Advisory:** Serve as a trusted advisor to key clients, providing tailored STCF solutions for corporate finance, project finance and other opportunities in the Nigerian market. Build and maintain strong relationships with local and international institutional investors/lenders, corporates, and counterparties to enhance market positioning.
* **Financial Performance and P\&L Oversight:** Manage the division’s profit and loss (P\&L) statement, budget and resource allocation. Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) such as revenue growth and return on capital, delivering consistent financial results in line with firm\-wide objectives and subsidiary goals.
* **Cross\-Functional Collaboration:** Partner with other divisions to integrate STCF solutions into broader client offerings. Contribute to group\-wide initiatives on sustainability, ESG integration, digital transformation, and alignment with the parent company’s global strategy.
* **Market Intelligence and Thought Leadership:** Stay abreast of industry trends, regulatory changes, and macroeconomic factors impacting STCF in Nigeria and Africa. Represent the firm at regional conferences, publish thought leadership pieces, and influence market standards through participation in local trade associations.

**Additional Responsibilities:**  



* Steer the direction of strategy and ensure an appropriate cascade to department and teams.
* Identify opportunities to provide STCF solutions to local, regional and international (existing and new) customers.
* Provide direction for developing STCF solutions for identified opportunities.
* Develop recommendations for product offerings and transactions.
* Develop relationships with new/existing clients towards increased market penetration and business expansion.
* Lead pitching opportunities in the STCF business.
* Work alongside and provide guidance where required with relevant stakeholders within the Group, in delivering STCF pitches to clients.
* Stay abreast of new developments in Structured Trade and Commodity Finance globally, regionally and in the local market.
* Ensure all requisite administration and filing matters for the STCF business follow statutory and regulatory requirements.
* Provide innovative financing solutions for clients, other departments and the Group’s senior management and colleagues.
* Lead the development of relevant strategic alliances and drive effective engagement with relevant stakeholders, including regulatory bodies.
* Provide guidance and update to the Board on all aspects of the Business including emerging trends and new market ventures, to ensure that actions/decisions are made in the best interests of the company.
* Create a business culture that encourages the use of ethical and sound corporate governance practices.
* Analyze and solve business problems to ensure the business \& Group’s existence and expansion.
* Delegate responsibilities and oversee the work of subordinates, offering direction and incentives to help them achieve their goals.
* Direct, manage, and develop employees, including hiring, orientation, training, counselling, and evaluation, and assisting them in their professional and personal development, as well as approving their discharge from the company’s service.
* Provide adequate support to the MD/CEO for market interface activities to increase the company’s visibility.
* Develop and implement policies and procedures for all STCF activities.
* Develop a deep understanding of clients' businesses, industries, financial performance, and strategic priorities.
* Maintain regular engagement with senior executives and key decision\-makers.
Deliver exceptional client experience while ensuring timely resolution of customer issues.  
* 

Requirements  

  



* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related field required; MBA, CFA, or advanced degree (e.g., JD, PhD in quantitative finance) are highly advantageous.
* Minimum 10\+ years in investment or corporate banking, global commodity trading, or development finance with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role within STCF or related areas (e.g., securitization, derivatives, or capital markets).
* Professional certifications such as ACCA, CFA, CIBN, or equivalent is desirable.
* Proven history of originating, financing and structuring commodity (physical or otherwise) transactions and managing teams in emerging markets, preferably in Africa.
* Deep knowledge of the West African commodity landscape, including Nigerian mining/oil sectors, regional agricultural export cycles and other physical commodities.
* Strong foundational knowledge of STCF, including institutional market practices and regulatory considerations.
* Deep knowledge of STCF instruments, including structuring techniques, pricing models, credit enhancement strategies and regulatory capital requirements.
* Experience with quantitative modelling, stress testing, and portfolio management is essential, with familiarity in regional asset classes (soft and hard commodities).
* Robust understanding of credit risk, market risk and risk controls, including practical application of credit assessment methodologies in commodities financing.
* Good understanding of Nigerian financial regulations (e.g., Investments and Securities Act, CBN FX regulations), international equivalents, and cross\-border trade regulations.
* Experience with ESG and sustainable finance frameworks in emerging markets is a plus.
* Proven success in driving revenue growth, managing P\&L, and navigating complex market dynamics in developing economies.
* Capacity to identify new market opportunities, translate business trends into actionable business strategies and leverage expertise to provide tailored solutions to target clients.
* Extensive client base and a network across global banking institutions, DFIs and potential investors.
* Demonstrated ability to inspire and lead diverse teams in a fast\-paced, high\-stakes environment.
* Strong decision\-making, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, with cultural awareness for operating in Nigeria.
* Strong foundational knowledge of physical commodities and structured trade financing, including institutional market practices and regulatory considerations.
* Strategic thinker with entrepreneurial mindset, excellent communication skills, goal\-orientation, resilience and the ability to thrive under pressure.
* High ethical standards, and cultural sensitivity for regional operations.
* Innovative thinker to develop bespoke financial solutions which will meet clients’ diverse needs.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to foster strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.  
* 

Benefits
  

N120,000,000\.00 – N150,000,000\.00 Annually \+ other benefits

job_title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Manager - Internal Only
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND
The IRC has been present in Nigeria since 2012 when the organization responded to flooding in Kogi state. In February 2014 the IRC moved into Adamawa State in NE Nigeria to provide humanitarian interventions through a multi-sectoral, integrated approach for conflict affected populations. IRC Nigeria now operates a country office in Abuja and field offices in Mubi and Yola of Adamawa State, Maiduguri and Monguno of Borno state and Damaturu of Yobe State. Currently, IRC Nigeria implements programs primary health care, nutrition, environmental health, women’s protection and empowerment, protection, child protection, education, food security & livelihoods.
Job Overview/Summary
The Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) Manager will provide operational, technical, and coordination support to the Emergency Preparedness and Response Coordinator (EPRCo) in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of emergency preparedness and response activities. The EPR Manager will actively contribute to strengthening IRC’s readiness to respond to emergencies and ensure timely, effective, and high-quality interventions. In this capacity, the EPR Manager will support the EPRCo in conducting key preparedness and response functions, including risk analysis, contingency planning, emergency assessments, response design, and implementation. The role will also involve working closely with sector teams, operations, and partners to ensure integrated and efficient program delivery.
In the absence of the EPRCo, or upon delegation, the EPR Manager will assume a leadership role and be responsible for overseeing emergency preparedness and response activities. This includes providing strategic direction, coordinating emergency response efforts, representing the organization in relevant coordination forums, and ensuring alignment with IRC standards, humanitarian principles, and donor requirements.
The EPR Manager will ensure continuity of operations during emergencies, support rapid decision-making, and maintain effective coordination both internally and externally. The role also requires proactive engagement in resource mobilization, reporting, and learning processes to strengthen the overall emergency response capacity of the country program.
The Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating the IRC’s emergency preparedness, contingency planning, and rapid response interventions. The role ensures timely, effective, and principled humanitarian responses to emergencies, aligned with IRC standards, donor requirements, and international humanitarian frameworks.
Major Responsibilities
The Emergency preparedness and Response manager will support the EPRCo in conducting the following activities and lead whenever the EPRCo is not available or through delegation by the EPRCo. Emergency Preparedness
Support the EPRCo in leading the development, review, and implementation of country-level emergency preparedness plans.
Conduct regular risk analysis, hazard mapping, and scenario planning.
Coordinate contingency planning across sectors (health, WASH, protection, ERD, nutrition).
Strengthen early warning systems and preparedness mechanisms.
Build staff capacity in emergency preparedness through training and simulations.
Emergency Response Management
Lead or coordinate rapid needs assessments in emergency situations.
Develop response strategies, including defining priorities, target populations, and modalities.
Ensure timely implementation of emergency projects in line with IRC standards.
Provide leadership during emergency activation and scale-up phases.
Coordinate emergency response teams and surge staff deployment. Program Quality & Implementation
Ensure all emergency interventions adhere to humanitarian principles (humanity, neutrality, impartiality, independence).
Monitor program quality, relevance, and accountability.
Integrate cross-cutting issues such as gender, protection, safeguarding, and inclusion.
Ensure compliance with IRC technical standards and sector guidelines. Coordination & Representation
Represents IRC in national and sub-national emergency coordination forums (e.g., clusters, working groups).
Strengthen partnerships with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, and local actors.
Support inter-agency coordination and joint response planning.
Resource Mobilization
Identify funding opportunities and contribute to proposal development.
Develop emergency concept notes, budgets, and logframes.
Liaise with donors and contribute to grant reporting
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)
Ensure effective MEAL systems for emergency response projects.
Track key performance indicators and ensure data-driven decision-making.
Promote accountability to affected populations through feedback mechanisms.
Document lessons learned and best practices. Logistics, Supply Chain & Operations Support
Coordinate with supply chain teams to ensure timely procurement and delivery of emergency supplies.
Support emergency pipeline management and stock prepositioning.
Ensure operational readiness for rapid response.
Team Management & Capacity Building
Supervise and mentor EPR staff and focal points.
Support recruitment and onboarding of emergency staff.
Build internal staff capacity on emergency response tools and approaches.
Program Management, Technical Quality, and Strategy
Program Management
Lead the design, planning, and implementation of emergency preparedness and response programs in line with organizational and cluster priorities.
Conduct and oversee rapid needs assessments and ensure timely analysis to inform response strategies.
Ensure efficient program delivery through strong coordination with government authorities, UN agencies, clusters, and partners.
Manage program budgets, including forecasting, expenditure tracking, and ensuring compliance with donor requirements.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track program progress, coverage, and effectiveness.
Produce high-quality internal and external reports, including situation reports (SitReps), donor updates, and operational briefs.
Identify operational risks and develop mitigation strategies to address access constraints, security issues, and supply chain disruptions.
Ensure timely mobilization and deployment of emergency response teams and resources.
Technical Quality
Ensure all emergency interventions meet global humanitarian standards, including Sphere Standards and the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS).
Provide technical oversight across sectors (e.g., Health, Nutrition, WASH, Shelter) to ensure quality and consistency of service delivery.
Promote evidence-based programming through the use of surveillance data, needs assessments, and monitoring systems.
Conduct regular field monitoring visits, technical reviews, and quality assurance checks to ensure program effectiveness.
Strengthen staff and partner capacity through training, mentorship, and supportive supervision on emergency protocols and technical guidelines.
Ensure accountability to affected populations (AAP) by establishing functional feedback and complaint mechanisms.
Lead post-distribution monitoring and evaluation activities to assess outcomes and inform program adjustments.
Ensure integration of cross-cutting issues such as protection, gender, and inclusion into program design and delivery.
Strategy
Lead the development and continuous adaptation of emergency preparedness and response strategies based on evolving context and risk analysis.
Conduct scenario planning (best-case, most likely, worst-case) to guide preparedness and contingency planning.
Ensure alignment of programs with national response frameworks, humanitarian response plans (HRP), and cluster strategies.
Drive prioritization of interventions based on severity, vulnerability, and available resources.
Promote a nexus approach by integrating emergency response with early recovery, resilience, and risk reduction initiatives.
Strengthening partnerships with local actors, government institutions, and community structures to support localization and sustainability.
Identify and promote innovative approaches, including digital tools, cash-based interventions, and remote programming modalities.
Lead learning and knowledge management processes, including after-action reviews and incorporation of lessons learned into future programming.
Program Development

Develop high-quality proposals, concept notes, and donor submissions.
Ensure alignment with donor priorities (ECHO, USAID, FCDO, UN).
Collaborate with MEAL, finance, and technical teams to ensure feasibility and impact.

Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth, where appropriate. As part of succession plan and nationalization goals, identify, train and develop capability and capacity of national staff to successfully transition role and responsibilities, by the end of assignment.
Adhere to and act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures and communicates through word and example a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies and regulations.
Research, Learning and Analysis
Lead the design and implementation of operational research, assessments, and analytical initiatives to inform evidence-based emergency preparedness and response programming.
Oversee needs assessments, baseline studies, and gap analyses, ensuring timely and accurate data collection to guide program decisions.
Analyze contextual data, trends, and risks (conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks, climate shocks) to support strategic planning and prioritization.

We are looking for a DevOps / Platform Engineer to own the systems that let our engineers ship safely and often. You will be the connective tissue between application code and production: building deployment pipelines, hardening our infrastructure, owning observability, and making the platform boring, predictable, and secure. Own CI/CD.

Run the data layer.
Keep our databases and caches healthy: backups, failover, capacity, and safe schema migrations coordinated with the backend team.
Own observability.
Build and curate dashboards, metrics, logs, and alerts so we detect problems before customers do. Drive incident response and blameless postmortems.
Harden security and compliance.

Plan for scale and resilience.
Capacity planning, cost optimization, load testing, and disaster-recovery drills.

Solid Linux, networking, and container fundamentals (Docker; orchestration a plus).
Hands-on CI/CD pipeline experience.
Experience operating relational databases and caches in production — backups, migrations, monitoring, and recovery.
Comfortable with observability tooling and leading incident response.
A scripting/automation language (e.g. Bash plus Go, Python, or TypeScript).
A security-first mindset and care for handling sensitive data correctly.

Async/queue-based worker systems.
Experience supporting mobile release pipelines.
Configuration management tooling.
Why Join Us
Real ownership of the platform from day one — your work directly shapes how the whole engineering org ships.
Meaningful problems: building reliable, secure financial infrastructure that expands access to credit.
A modern, fully-codified stack with no legacy click-ops to untangle.
A team that treats reliability and security as core engineering work.
About Roja
Roja is a peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform. We connect borrowers and lenders through a mobile app, a customer-facing web app, and a staff operations dashboard, all backed by a single API. Because we move money and handle sensitive customer data, we operate under strict regulatory expectations — reliability, security, and auditability are first-class product concerns, not afterthoughts.
We run a modern, fully codified cloud stack: a Go backend with background workers, a managed relational database and cache, web frontends, and a cross-platform mobile app. Our infrastructure is defined as code and deployed through automated pipelines.

Perform regular site visits to verify work progress and ensure material usage aligns with budget allocations.
Identify and mitigate commercial risks that could impact project timelines or margins.

Maintain rigorous document control for all commercial agreements and site variations.
Ensure all procurement and billing processes are standardized and transparent.

### **Job descriptions \& requirements**

  

  

**About the Company**


We're a boutique Canadian marine operations consultancy. Our mission: solving the challenges that move global trade.


We work across three core service lines: marine operations consulting and terminal support, where we act as a seamless extension of our clients' marine, trading, and logistics desks; shipbroking, where we source vessels, negotiate contracts, and follow shipments through operationally; and digital solutions, where we build bespoke software tools for charterers and ship owners.


Our clients are primarily large North American oil and gas companies, mining firms, and ship owners who move product via bulk marine transportation — Fortune 100 energy firms navigating vessel chartering and cargo logistics, and ship owners seeking better tools to analyze fleet economics and voyage performance.


Since 1988, we have delivered on brokerage and consultancy mandates for clients ranging from Fortune 100 companies to resource and trading firms and government organizations. We have facilitated more than 2,500 bulk liquid and dry bulk commodity shipments, moving over $1 billion in freight, and we are growing — in headcount, in service lines, and in ambition.


**OUR COMPANY VALUES**


* **Work to Be the Best**
* + **Bias for Action**
* **Helpfulness**
* **Integrity \& Radical Candour**
* **Clarity \& Accountability**
* **Innovation**
* **Attention to Detail**

We're a fully remote team of 10, including roles across Operations, Software Engineering, and Creative. Our Canadian team is spread across Toronto, Montreal, and Calgary, with an Operations team in the Philippines and a Software Engineering team in Tunisia.

  

  

**About the Role**


We're looking for a **remote Marine Operations Specialist** to become a key domain expert on our team — owning marine operations support, contributing to client engagements, and helping build the maritime knowledge base that lets this business scale.


As we grow and expand across maritime services and technology, we're building out our maritime knowledge base with real\-world expertise.


Day\-to\-day, the work is a genuine mix: routine marine operations support forms the foundation — vessel lineups, voyage itineraries, client calls, port coordination — and in the capacity that creates, you'll take on terminal projects, market research, shipbroking support, client presentations, and cross\-functional advisory work with our Software Engineering and Creative teams. We embrace AI and technology\-assisted ways of working — not to replace expertise, but to help you work smarter and do more.

  

  

**Our IDEAL CANDIDATE** brings 5 to 7 years of maritime experience — from port or terminal operations, vessel operations, ship management, chartering, or a commercial shipping environment. A background in tanker or bulk liquids operations \- LPG, LNG, chemical, crude, or product tanker \- is a strong advantage. You understand how the industry actually works: how vessels move, how ports function, how cargo gets handled, and how the commercial and operational sides connect.

  

  

**Reporting Structure:** This position sits on the Operations team, working closely with the CEO, Director of Operations, and Operations Analyst, and coordinating with the Software Engineering and Creative teams on digital product development and marketing content. This role reports directly to the Director of Operations.


You'll be doing things like:

  

  

* **Day\-to\-Day Client Coordination \& Vessel Tracking:** sending out daily vessel lineups and voyage itineraries; leading Tuesday and Thursday client calls; coordinating with port agents for documentation (PDAs, FDAs); tracking loading operations, cargo movements, and vessel schedules; monitoring berth management and certificate validity; ensuring nothing falls through the cracks in the weekly export cycle
* **Marine Operations Support \& Process Improvement:** reviewing and refining Excel templates and operational tools for accuracy and completeness; defining and documenting marine operating procedures and SOPs for current and legacy work streams; supporting data capture and entry for bunker consumption, fuel pricing, noon reports, and vessel performance figures; identifying process improvements and consolidating fragmented work streams into a single function
* **Terminal Projects \& Port\-Specific Deliverables:** developing terminal handbooks and operational procedures for new client terminal projects; preparing tariff schedules and port\-specific documentation; conducting marine operations assessments and providing expert recommendations; addressing technical operational questions on vessel performance, dual\-fuel accounting, and cargo handling
* **Shipbroking \& Commercial Support:** conducting vessel availability research and supporting fixture documentation; preparing charterparty documentation and correspondence; supporting the CEO on shipbroking activity, including owner outreach and cargo placement; maintaining internal reference materials on vessel types, trade lanes, and port characteristics
* **Vessel Market Research \& Trade Lane Analysis:** researching vessel types, markets, and trade lanes; analysing handy\-size vessel segments and LPG market dynamics by region; monitoring freight market developments and vessel rates; supporting disport cost optimisation calculations and voyage planning analysis; supporting business case development on topics like hull cleaning economics and ocean freight calculations
* **Client Presentations \& Polished Reporting:** contributing to monthly client PowerPoint presentations with maritime operational insights; translating technical marine content into clear, accessible language for non\-specialist audiences; developing proposals and one\-to\-two page pitch materials, including for new digital product offerings; preparing polished reports and commercial briefings for client and external audiences
* **Internal Knowledge Building \& Cross\-Functional Advisory:** advising the Software Engineering team on maritime business logic for digital tools and relational databases, including data structures for vessel, cargo, and operational datasets; contributing maritime expertise to marketing content direction and social media strategy; documenting operational frameworks and building reference materials to strengthen the organization's collective knowledge base; onboarding and educating team members on maritime topics as the organization grows

**Skills \& Qualifications**


* 5 to 7 years of prior experience in roles like Marine Operations Coordinator, Port Operations Specialist, Vessel Operator, Marine Superintendent, Chartering Assistant, Maritime Analyst, Deck Officer, Chief Mate, Marine Engineer, ideally in ship owning, ship management, port or terminal operations, or commercial shipping.
* Solid working knowledge of maritime operations — port and terminal operations, vessel operations, bulk shipping, tanker operations, or commercial chartering — and how vessels, ports, and supply chains actually function
* Strong analytical capability, comfortable working with data, drawing conclusions, and presenting findings clearly
* Ability to research and synthesise independently, producing concise outputs from complex or technical material
* Proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel, able to produce professional materials and conduct structured analysis
* Strong verbal and written English, able to lead client calls and produce polished correspondence and reports
* Comfortable using AI tools to support research, analysis, and deliverable production
* Generalist mindset, drawn to the breadth of the industry rather than one narrow technical domain
* Passionate about maritime and curious about how the industry is evolving
* Self\-directed and organised, able to manage multiple priorities without constant oversight
* Collaborative and communicative, with the professionalism to work effectively across a small, senior team

Bonus if you also have:


* Exposure to shipbroking, chartering, or freight market activity
* Familiarity with maritime regulations and standard commercial documentation (charterparties, bills of lading, port documentation)

Experience in tanker or bulk liquids shipping * \- LPG, LNG, chemical tanker, crude, or product tanker operations
* Education from a maritime university or formal maritime training program
* Industry contacts within maritime operations or commercial shipping
* Experience advising on or contributing to digital tool development for maritime applications
* Familiarity with our tools: Microsoft Office (including Teams), ClickUp, Claude, Copilot

**Position Details**


**Working Hours:** 7AM\-4PM or 8AM\-5PM Toronto time (Eastern Time). Adjusts with Daylight Saving Time.


**Employment Type:** Full\-time (40 hours/week), Exclusivity Preferred


**Education:** A degree in maritime studies, marine engineering, logistics, supply chain, or a related field is preferred, but relevant work experience and demonstrated maritime expertise are what matter here.


**Level:** Upper\-Intermediate to Senior (5–7 years of relevant experience)


**Compensation:** \~CAD $1,102–$1,322 (NGN 1\.5M–1\.8M)/month, based on experience and region. Structured as a Consultant Agreement (independent contractor), meaning you'll be responsible for your own taxes, benefits, and insurance.

  

  

**Benefits of working with us:**


* Work directly with a Canadian maritime consultancy serving Fortune 100 energy clients and ship owners globally
* 100% remote

‍* + ️ 8 hours a day, 5 days a week
* Above\-market compensation for your region
* 15 days paid vacation, Canadian public holidays, plus 2 local holiday swap days
* Be a key domain expert on the team — your knowledge shapes client work, internal tools, and company direction from day one
* Real exposure to complex, high\-stakes maritime engagements across consulting, shipbroking, and digital products
* Direct access to the CEO and senior leadership, with real room to grow as the firm scales

The Area Business Manager will coordinate sales, collections and distribution operations in the area they are assigned for the direct distribution of Sun King Solar products sold on Pay-As-You-Basis (also called and recognized as “EasyBuy” Business unit) through a network of agents called as “Energy Officer”. Hire & retain Energy Officers: Hire, train and maintain a team of at least 40 Sun King Energy Officers in the area. Use multiple avenues for finding the right talent to sell Sun King EasyBuy products with the help of village influencers such as the village heads, teachers, religious heads, doctors, farmers and others, as applicable. Create a reputation and goodwill for the mission of Sun King to provide clean, affordable and reliable source of energy in their areas.
Training of Energy Officers: Provide training to the Energy Officers on several aspects of the business such as sales, collections, product, technical, inventory and logistics related. Ensure that they are fully supervised in the best professional manner demonstrating highest levels of integrity, ethics and professionalism while dealing with customers.
Provide role clarity to Energy Officers: Provide complete clarity to Energy Officers related to their day to day tasks, sales & collections plans, routes and targets. This includes, ensuring Energy Officers have sales route/area to sell in, they know on how to demonstrate and sell Sun King products, they have the confidence to be able to present and resolve basic customer queries on the spot and they have access to Area Business Manager at all times in case of questions and concerns.
Daily field visits: Have a weekly touchpoint with every Energy Officer in your area – either through in-person meetings, making a sale to the customer in your area or having a call. Resolve all possible issues faced by the Energy Officers and report them to your Regional Business Manager, every week. Ensure that first 5 sales of each Energy Officer is done along with the Area Business Manager in the area, by each Energy Officer to ensure that the core sales and collection process is fully understood by each Energy Officer.
Work with Energy Officers: Conduct joint field work with a group of Energy Officers to provide sales and collection training on a weekly basis and drive EO engagement. This includes doing night activations, market activations, visiting local communities and gatherings such as SACCOs, Self Help groups, retail centers and markets to make group sales.
Exceed your sales & collections targets: Meet or exceed sales and collection targets established on 2nd of every month by your Regional Business Manager. Provide daily, weekly updates on sales, EO recruitments, Customer issues and resolutions, in alignment with your Regional Business Manager.
Drive robust field sales processes: Review collection progress with your Energy Officers daily and provide adequate training to them on driving better collections in your areas. This includes, customer and area profiling, ensuring regular and timely collection follow-ups, resolving customer issues to ensure they make payments and ultimately repossessing the systems as a last recourse in case the customer defaults.
Remain externally focused: Keep an eye on companies selling similar products within your area and ensure you take adequate measures to protect and grow our business from pressures. Pre-inform your management team and take measures to ensure Sun King remains a paramount brand name in Solar products for your area.
Resolve customer issues: Provide world-class customer service to your customers as it relates to product delivery, training on how to use and make payments, installation, after sales warranty issues. Ensure that you work with your Energy Officers to establish clear expectations and processes to resolve all customer issues within 24 hours.
Control Marketing & Other spend: Provide adequate marketing materials & equipment (such as smartphones) necessary to all your Energy Officers. Ensure we get maximum return on investment for all the costs we incur in areas of marketing, supply chain, store maintenance and smartphone issuance.
Review meetings with Energy Officers: Conduct weekly table meetings with Energy Officers and ensure that you have RBM present in those meetings to resolve any outstanding customers or EO issues. Coordinate, plan and organize the meeting to have maximum attendance and progress. Recognize outstanding performers from time to time and ensure the motivation of Energy Officers is maintained at an all-time high.
Grow Retail presence: Ensure the retail network in your Area grows with the help of the Cluster leaders, hired under you.
You might be a strong candidate if you
Have a degree in a Business-related field OR equivalent and at least 3 years hands on experience in Sales.
Have excellent Computer knowledge with comprehensive knowledge of Excel and PowerPoint
Have extensive Customer Care experience
Are innovative, and you think out of the box
Are skilled in Planning, Organizing, Prioritizing, maximizing value and see the big picture
Are able to skillfully builds relations, works on internal & external relationships
Listen well, coaches others and is disciplined in their learning practice
Have Operation Excellence (Keeps promise, seeks to be informed and gives excellent Customer Satisfaction
Have knowledge of the territory
What Sun King Offers
Professional growth in a dynamic, rapidly expanding, high-social-impact industry
An open-minded, collaborative culture with enthusiastic colleagues driven by the challenge of innovation and making a profound impact on people and the planet.
A truly multicultural experience: you will have the chance to work with and learn from people from different geographies, nationalities, and backgrounds.
Structured, tailored learning and development programs that help you become a better leader, manager, and professional through the Sun King Center for Leadership.
About Sun King
Sun King is the world’s leading off-grid solar energy company, combining cutting-edge product design, fintech, and field operations to deliver energy access for the 1.8 billion people who live without an affordable and reliable electric-grid connection.
Sun King has built a new kind of energy utility: distributed, green, customer-centric, and affordable. We bring clean, reliable, decentralized energy directly into people’s lives — from solar kits that provide first-time energy access to multi-kilowatt systems that serve both off-grid users and grid-connected customers powering larger homes, schools, hospitals, farms, offices, and light manufacturing.
Already, 25 million homes and businesses rely on Sun King for electricity supply and the appliances and services it enables: lighting, televisions, fans, refrigeration, and smartphones.
Sun King combines energy generation, energy-efficient appliances, installation, and financing into one seamless offering. Think of it as a distributed utility, designed for wherever energy is needed and designed to scale with its users as incomes and energy needs grow.
Sun King makes solar products affordable to low-income households and businesses via ‘pay-as-you-go’ (PAYG) purchase financing. Sun King installs solar after customers pay a small deposit. Customers then make small, manageable payments of as little as US $0.14 a day via mobile money or cash.
Instead of paying for expensive, polluting, and health-damaging kerosene for lighting or diesel for power, customers unlock savings through accessing solar power and after one to two years of payments, customers own their solar equipment outright.
Sun King collects payments digitally through mobile money systems and its 35,000 field agents — over 1 million payments each day. To date, Sun King has extended more than $1.4 billion in PAYG loans to customers.
Sun King began by powering homes and businesses with solar systems delivered through PAYG financing. Now, we’re using the same model to make smartphones and clean cooking equipment affordable: helping households connect to the digital economy and transition from wood-based fuels to modern, sustainable alternatives.
Sun King employs 3,500 full-time staff in 14 countries, with specialties spanning product design, data science, logistics, customer service, sales, software, operations, and more — all with a passion to serve off-grid families. Sun King is committed to gender diversity in the workplace. Women represent 42% of Sun King’s workforce.

Job Description
Reports To: Managing Director
Industry: Natural gas / midstream energy
Position Overview
The Director of Marketing will lead the strategic development and execution of marketing and commercial initiatives to drive adoption of natural gas products (LNG, CNG, and NGLs) across Nigeria. This role focuses on demand creation, customer acquisition, market expansion, and revenue growth across industrial, commercial, power, and mobility sectors. The ideal candidate combines deep knowledge of the Nigerian gas value chain with strong commercial instincts, stakeholder engagement capabilities, and experience in energy or infrastructure markets.
Key Responsibilities
1. Market Strategy & Growth:
Develop and execute a national marketing strategy for natural gas products (LNG, CNG, piped gas).
Identify and prioritize target sectors (manufacturing, power generation, transport, telecoms, FMCG, etc.).
Drive gas adoption strategies aligned with Nigeria's Decade of Gas initiative.
Analyze market trends, competitor positioning, and pricing dynamics.
2. Customer Acquisition & Offtake Development:
Lead customer acquisition efforts to secure long-term gas offtake agreements.
Build and manage a pipeline of industrial and commercial customers.
Work closely with Business Development to structure commercial offers and contracts.
Support negotiations of GSAs (Gas Sales Agreements) and supply frameworks.
3. Product Positioning & Value Proposition:
Develop clear value propositions for LNG, CNG, and virtual pipeline solutions.
Position natural gas as a cost-effective and cleaner alternative to diesel and fuel oil.
Design sector-specific solutions (e.g., embedded power, captive energy systems, mobility fuel).
4. Branding, Communications & Campaigns:
Lead brand positioning as a trusted gas supplier and energy partner.
Oversee marketing campaigns, digital presence, and thought leadership initiatives.
Represent the company at industry forums, conferences, and government engagements.
Develop marketing collateral, case studies, and client success stories.
5. Stakeholder Engagement:
Engage with regulators, industry bodies, and government agencies (e.g., NMDPRA, NNPC stakeholders).
Build relationships with EPC contractors, OEMs, and equipment suppliers.
Collaborate with financing partners to support customer conversion (e.g., gas conversion CAPEX support models).
6. Commercial & Revenue Management:
Develop pricing strategies in coordination with finance and operations teams.
Monitor sales performance, margins, and customer profitability.
Establish KPIs for market penetration, conversion rates, and revenue growth.
7. Cross-Functional Leadership:
Collaborate with operations, supply chain, and engineering teams to align supply capabilities with market demand.
Support project development (e.g., LNG plants, CNG stations) with market insights and demand validation.
Lead and mentor the marketing and commercial team.
Qualifications & Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Engineering, Economics, or related field; MBA preferred.
10–15+ years of experience in energy, oil & gas, or infrastructure sectors.
Proven track record in B2B marketing, commercial strategy, or gas sales.
Strong understanding of the Nigerian gas market, including LNG/CNG distribution models.
Experience working with industrial clients and large-scale energy users.
Strategic thinking and market development; strong commercial and negotiation skills.
Deep knowledge of gas pricing and supply structures; stakeholder management and government relations.
Leadership and team development; data-driven decision-making.
Preferred: experience with virtual pipeline (LNG/CNG trucking) models; familiarity with gas-to-power and embedded generation; exposure to carbon reduction / ESG positioning in energy markets.
Compensation: base + performance bonus tied to gas sales volumes and revenue; long-term and deal-based incentives may apply (discuss with HR).
Key targets (indicative): secure 3–6 anchor customers with multi-year contracts; drive plant utilization and diesel-to-gas conversion; build pipeline ahead of capacity.

Job Description: Senior Internal Auditor (Retail & IT Systems)
Location:
Lagos, Nigeria
Directorate:
Group Internal Audit / Governance Directorate
Reports To:
Group Managing Director / Audit Committee
Position Type:
Full-Time
About the Role
The Managing Directorate is seeking a highly vigilant, tech-savvy, and eagle-eyed
Senior Internal Auditor (Retail & IT Systems)
. This role is a critical pillar of our institutional governance, designed to safeguard assets across our luxury retail, real estate, hospitality, and family office portfolio.
The ideal candidate bridges the gap between traditional financial auditing and modern IT/ERP systems auditing. You will be responsible for ensuring that our digital workflows (ERP, Point of Sale, and Supply Chain systems) perfectly match our physical inventory, cash flows, and corporate policies. You will move our audit functions away from retrospective paperwork into proactive, system-driven risk mitigation.
Key Responsibilities1. ERP & IT Systems Auditing (The Digital Infrastructure)
ERP Controls Review:
Audit, test, and challenge the internal controls built into the Group’s ERP system (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or Odoo). Ensure user access permissions are properly segregated to prevent fraud (Segregation of Duties).
Data Integrity & IT Security:
Audit data flows between frontline points of sale (POS) systems, e-commerce platforms, and back-end accounting software. Ensure zero data leakage or unauthorized data manipulation.
System Vulnerability Mapping:
Identify operational loopholes in digital procurement, automated stock valuations, and payment gateways.
2. Luxury Retail & Operational Audits (The Physical Infrastructure)
Inventory & Shrinkage Control:
Design and execute foolproof audit programs to track luxury home goods and hospitality stock from importation/local procurement to warehousing and final sale. Minimize shrinkage, damage, and theft.
Margin & Pricing Audits:
Audit off-plan real estate sales records, retail discounting structures, and bistro inventory costs to ensure actual margins match strategic financial models.
Procurement & Asset Financing Scrutiny:
Review vendor selections, contract enforcement, and asset financing deployments (e.g., credit lines, heavy equipment/vehicle purchasing) to ensure absolute transparency and policy compliance.
3. Forensic Governance & Reporting
System-Driven Investigations:
Lead forensic reviews when discrepancies arise, utilizing data analytics tools to trace anomalies directly back to system logs and user IDs.
Institutionalized Reporting:
Draft highly structured, objective audit reports for the Group MD and Board. Reports must move away from generic summaries and provide specific, data-backed findings and actionable remediation timelines.
Candidate Requirements
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field.
Professional Certifications (At least one is non-negotiable):
CISA
(Certified Information Systems Auditor) – Highly Preferred for the IT side.
ACA / ACCA
(Chartered Accountant) – Essential for the financial/operational side.
CIA
(Certified Internal Auditor) is an added advantage.
Experience:
4–7 years of experience, with at least 3 years explicitly focused on
retail operations
and
IT/ERP auditing
. Experience working with top-tier audit firms (Big 4) or structured multi-unit retail chains is highly desirable.
Technical Skills:
Deep familiarity with retail ERPs, advanced Excel, SQL, or data analytics software (like ACL, Idea, or PowerBI) to pull and analyze large datasets directly from systems.
Mindset:
Uncompromising integrity, highly analytical, detail-obsessed, and capable of standing firm on corporate policy.

Proforce Galaxies Limited is an advanced space and satellite technology company focused on upstream, midstream, and downstream space operations.
